articles.title: Rs 3-crore Defender, horse race with SUV prize, 150 dishes: Anant Singh goes all out for daughter's wedding
articles.summary: Mokama MLA Anant Singh plans lavish Nov 25 wedding in Ladma: 4 lakh guests, luxury cars, horse race, 150+ dishes, artists and VIP invites.
articles.body: PATNA: A Rs 3-crore Land Rover Defender for the bridegroom, a BMW worth around Rs 1 crore for the younger son, a wedding venue spread over more than 10 bighas, a horse race with an SUV as the top prize and a menu boasting over 150 dishes.If weddings are about making a statement, Mokama MLA Anant Singh is ensuring his daughter’s big day will be difficult to miss. Add Bollywood and Bhojpuri artists, six models from Dubai and invitations for some of the country’s biggest political names, and the celebrations in Ladma village have become an event with all eyes on it.Known for his flamboyant lifestyle and larger-than-life public persona, Singh is preparing for the Nov 25 wedding of his younger daughter, Shivangi Singh, to Rishikesh Kumar alias Ankit, son of commandant Ranvijay Kumar of Krishnanagar in Bihta, Patna. Rishikesh holds an MBA degree and has lived in the United States for around 11 years.The luxury Defender, estimated to cost between Rs 2.5 crore and Rs 3 crore, has already reached Ladma. The BMW, worth around Rs 1 crore, is for Singh’s youngest son Abhinav, whose ‘janeu’ ceremony will be held alongside the wedding. The vehicles have become a talking point in the village even before the wedding festivities have gathered full pace.The wedding venue is being developed across more than 10 bighas, while a separate ground spread over nearly 12 bighas is being prepared for the horse-racing competition. The scale of the arrangements has prompted Singh to plan for around four lakh visitors, with preparations allowing for the possibility of even more guests.The wedding decorations are being planned on a similarly imposing scale. A nearly 30-foot-high stage, inspired by Jaipur’s Patrakar Chauraha, is being built for the ‘jaimala’ ceremony. Flowers are being sourced from China and Bengaluru, decorative materials from different parts of the country, and tent workers have been brought in from Mau in Uttar Pradesh. A specialised event company has been entrusted with the work.Puneet Kumar, Singh’s eldest son-in-law, said the Defender was chosen by Shivangi and gifted to her on her birthday. She completed her schooling in Delhi and post-graduation from Delhi University.The family has a history of elaborate wedding arrangements. “I was married to Raj Nandini, eldest daughter of Singh, in 2015. In my wedding, only parking was made on around 4 bighas of land,” said the son-in-law.The horse race, scheduled for Nov 25 from 2pm to 4pm, is expected to draw riders from Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, Gujarat, Haryana and other states. Manish Kumar, an associate of Singh, said the winner would receive an SUV, the runner-up a motorcycle and the third-place finisher a scooter.Food, too, is being treated as an event in itself. The menu will feature more than 150 varieties, ranging from traditional Bihari preparations to dishes from other states. Sweets will include kaju katli and Silao khaja, the Nalanda speciality known for its distinctive 52-layer structure.Singh has also expressed his wish to invite PM Narendra Modi, former Bihar CM Nitish Kumar, RJD president Lalu Prasad and Tejashwi Prasad Yadav. articles.title: Assam man hacks woman inside car, dumps body in ditch near temple
articles.summary: Assam: Driver Pradeep Taye arrested for allegedly killing Jeena Baishya and dumping her body in Khanapara; vehicle and machete seized, probe ongoing.
articles.body: GUWAHATI: Police arrested a driver on Monday for allegedly hacking a woman to death and dumping her body in a sack in Khanapara.The accused, Pradeep Taye (45) of Dhemaji district, and the deceased, Jeena Baishya (32) of Koinadhara, were allegedly in an extramarital relationship for 10 years. Police suspect frequent disputes between them may have led to the murder.Baishya’s body was recovered near a temple in Khanapara on Saturday. Her husband, Jeetu Baishya, lodged a complaint at Basistha Police Station earlier that day, following which a murder case was registered.“The woman’s body was recovered near Ganesh temple on Saturday. On the same day, before the recovery, her husband had lodged a complaint at Basistha police station. A case was registered under the relevant sections of the law pertaining to murder,” said Basistha OC Kapil Pathak.Pathak said the case initially appeared to be a no-clue murder, but circumstantial and other evidence led to Taye’s arrest in Koinadhara.“Following the arrest, we seized a vehicle, the machete used in the crime and other items that were connected to this incident,” he said.Police allege that Taye picked up Baishya from Basistha on the day of the incident and drove her around for several hours. He allegedly took her to an isolated spot near the temple around 8 pm, attacked her with a weapon inside the vehicle and dumped her body in a nearby ditch.Police said the investigation is continuing. articles.title: Caso amoroso de chefe da Nvidia vira preocupação nos EUA | G1
articles.standfirst: Jensen Huang está sendo investigado por sua própria empresa devido a um relacionamento extraconjugal com uma mulher que, segundo alegações, seria uma espiã chinesa.
articles.summary: Jensen Huang está sendo investigado por sua própria empresa devido a um relacionamento extraconjugal com uma mulher que, segundo alegações, seria uma espiã chinesa.
articles.body:
O mundo da tecnologia passou o dia digerindo a notícia extraordinária de que Jensen Huang — o carismático CEO da Nvidia , empresa multibilionária — está sendo investigado pela sua própria companhia devido a um caso extraconjugal com uma mulher que, segundo alegações, seria uma espiã chinesa.

O suposto envolvimento amoroso de Huang com Alice Huang , ex-CEO de uma empresa de centros de dados sediada em Singapura, gerou repercussões que vão muito além de sua família — que, sem dúvida, vive seu próprio turbilhão emocional —, colocando-nos diante de uma encruzilhada onde tecnologia, geopolítica e segurança nacional se cruzam.

Em suma, trata-se da intensa rivalidade entre os Estados Unidos e a China, bem como da questão de saber se Jensen Huang traiu não apenas sua esposa, mas também os EUA.

Os EUA estão envolvidos em uma disputa acirrada com a China pelo desenvolvimento dos melhores modelos de inteligência artificial (IA).

Jensen Huang, CEO da Nvidia, durante evento em Washington — Foto: Julia Demaree Nikhinson/AP Photo

"Quem vencer na IA, vence", como diz o presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump . Ele acredita que o país com a tecnologia de IA mais dominante será o que mais se beneficiará dela e, por fim, se tornará o mais poderoso do mundo. É bem possível que ele tenha razão.

A Nvidia fabrica os melhores chips do setor para IA — tanto que a demanda superou sua capacidade de oferta.

A empresa define seus preços de acordo com essa realidade: uma única unidade de seu equipamento mais recente para centros de dados custa a partir de US$ 50 mil, o equivalente a cerca de R$ 275,5 mil. Uma instalação de médio ou grande porte pode contar com centenas dessas unidades.

O governo dos EUA impôs, inicialmente, uma proibição à exportação dos dispositivos mais recentes da Nvidia , visando impedir que a China tirasse proveito de suas capacidades superiores. Posteriormente, as regras foram flexibilizadas.

A Bloomberg noticiou que a empresa adquiriu, em novembro de 2025, tecnologias da Nvidia avaliadas em bilhões de dólares. A Megaspeed nega que os produtos tenham sido utilizados de forma ilícita.

Por sua vez, Jensen Huang tem feito um intenso trabalho de lobby pela flexibilização das regras de exportação entre os dois países. Ele argumenta — contrariando a opinião predominante — que a corrida pela IA não é algo determinante e que não seria um problema se a China se tornasse dependente da tecnologia americana.

"O presidente Trump quer que os EUA vençam, e o presidente Xi quer que a China vença; é possível que ambos alcancem seus objetivos", declarou ele à BBC no ano passado.

É seguro afirmar que nenhum dos dois países enxerga a situação dessa maneira.

As questões complexas que a Nvidia agora precisa tentar responder incluem se Alice obteve acesso privilegiado à tecnologia mais recente da empresa — de forma deliberada ou não — por meio de Jensen; e, em caso afirmativo, se ela compartilhou essas informações com Pequim ou com terceiros.

Não se sabe quando o relacionamento entre eles começou ou terminou, mas existem inúmeras fotos e vídeos de Jensen e Alice juntos em eventos. É plausível que tenham passado longos períodos a sós, e Jensen já mencionou que está sempre atento ao seu trabalho.

A China nega que ela estivesse envolvida em espionagem.

O interesse em espionagem econômica não é algo novo nem exclusivo da China. Contudo, muitos países ocidentais afirmam que a China pratica essa atividade em larga escala, utilizando uma combinação de ferramentas tecnológicas e agentes infiltrados em diversas organizações, inclusive empresas privadas.

Caso a China obtenha acesso a um volume significativo de chips da Nvidia — seja para utilizá-los diretamente ou para desmontá-los e aprender a fabricar suas próprias versões —, isso enfureceria o governo Trump, que busca manter suas tecnologias de inteligência artificial sob estrito controle.

Alguns modelos, inclusive, não foram compartilhados com o AI Safety Institute , sediado no Reino Unido , sob a justificativa de que seriam potencialmente perigosos demais. Os EUA não querem que terceiros obtenham vantagem competitiva ou façam mau uso de suas inovações.

Outro ponto potencialmente explosivo diz respeito a eventuais informações sobre segurança nacional às quais Jensen Huang possa ter tido acesso.

Ele é uma figura que transita no alto escalão da elite norte-americana — uma das poucas pessoas que, provavelmente, poderia entrar na Casa Branca sem aviso prévio e tomar um chá com Trump. Ele possui influência, acesso e amizades poderosas. É perfeitamente possível que segredos tenham sido compartilhados com ele.

A Nvidia afirma que, até o momento, não há evidências de que ele tenha repassado qualquer informação, e a empresa iniciou uma investigação interna. Huang declarou que irá colaborar e deseja manter seu cargo — embora, no mínimo, ele tenha violado o próprio código de conduta da Nvidia , que proíbe que integrantes da empresa mantenham relacionamentos com clientes.

No momento, ele conta com o apoio tanto do conselho da Nvidia quanto de Trump, que o descreveu como "honrado" e especulou que deveria haver uma razão para o que aconteceu. Em outras palavras, ele não está deixando seu amigo executivo do setor de tecnologia na mão.

Trump afirmou que o FBI está investigando o relacionamento entre o executivo e a suposta espiã.

"Eu fiz essa pergunta: 'Você fazia ideia de que ela era uma espiã?'. Ele respondeu: 'Eu não fazia ideia de que ela era uma espiã', e eu realmente acredito nele", disse o presidente a repórteres.

O preço das ações da Nvidia caiu, mas não despencou de forma catastrófica, o que sugere que os acionistas também não estão abandonando a empresa sob sua gestão.

Uma indústria de IA com uma Nvidia enfraquecida seria, sem dúvida, uma indústria mais lenta.

E, na verdade, não existe um sucessor natural pronto para assumir o lugar de Jensen, caso ele seja forçado a sair.

Huang comanda a Nvidia há mais de 30 anos — para muitos, ele é a própria Nvidia . Ele conduziu a empresa por diversas crises, e foi uma decisão sua fazer com que a companhia priorizasse IA muito antes de isso se tornar uma tendência.

Ele é conhecido por ser um chefe exigente, que espera que sua equipe trabalhe longas jornadas e mantenha um alto padrão. Há relatos de que ele convocava reuniões com todos os funcionários apenas para repreender publicamente aqueles que haviam cometido erros. Ele justificava isso dizendo que era uma forma de evitar que outros cometessem as mesmas falhas — mas é fácil imaginar como se sentiam aqueles que eram alvo dessas críticas.

Enquanto aguarda a conclusão da investigação sobre suas ações, Huang deve esperar que, apesar de ele próprio não ter tolerado os erros de seus colegas no passado, eles sejam compreensivos em relação às suas próprias falhas.

E ele também precisa conviver com a ironia de ter sido, possivelmente, desmascarado não por uma operação sofisticada de alta tecnologia, mas pelo truque mais antigo que existe: uma armadilha de sedução.

articles.title: Chuva forte provoca alagamentos de ruas e casas em São Francisco | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo o coordenador da Defesa Civil Municipal, a tempestade começou por volta das 18h e foram registrados cerca de 72 milímetros de chuva em apenas uma hora.
articles.summary: Segundo o coordenador da Defesa Civil Municipal, a tempestade começou por volta das 18h e foram registrados cerca de 72 milímetros de chuva em apenas uma hora.
articles.body:
Uma forte chuva deixou ruas e casas alagadas em São Francisco , no Norte de Minas, no fim da tarde desta segunda-feira (9).

Segundo o coordenador da Defesa Civil Municipal, Romenig Barbosa Martins, a tempestade começou por volta das 18h, quando foram registrados cerca de 72 milímetros de chuva em apenas uma hora. Depois, a precipitação continuou, mas com menor intensidade. Em algumas residências, a água chegou a atingir um metro de altura.

Entre os bairros mais afetados estão Sagrada Família, Centro, São José, Santo Antônio e Jardim Realito, onde mais de 20 famílias receberam atendimento da Defesa Civil. Os moradores deixaram as casas durante a tempestade e retornaram depois que o nível da água baixou. Apenas duas famílias permanecem abrigadas em casas de parentes.

Casas foram alagadas em São Francisco — Foto: Defesa Civil/Divulgação

Ninguém ficou ferido, mas houve prejuízos materiais, com perdas de móveis e eletrodomésticos.

Ainda de acordo com a Defesa Civil, as aulas foram suspensas nesta terça-feira (10) no CEMEI Monteiro Lobato e no CEMEI Pedacinho do Céu. As unidades ficaram alagadas durante a tempestade e passarão por um trabalho de limpeza.

Nesta manhã, agentes da Defesa Civil vão percorrer as regiões mais afetadas para avaliar a extensão dos danos e realizar vistorias. A orientação é que, ao identificar qualquer sinal de risco, os moradores deixem imediatamente os imóveis e as áreas alagadas.

articles.title: Mumbai local train stabbing: Accused claims real 'killer' fled, says he was a bystander
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Roshan Suvarna, 30, arrested for allegedly stabbing 22-year-old Mayank Lohar to death inside a moving local train, has sought bail, claiming he
articles.body: MUMBAI: Roshan Suvarna, 30, arrested for allegedly stabbing 22-year-old Mayank Lohar to death inside a moving local train, has sought bail, claiming he was merely a bystander injured while trying to stop a fight between Lohar and an unidentified man.Suvarna's plea says he intervened in the quarrel, suffered injuries, and was falsely implicated after the alleged attacker fled. Lohar's family has opposed bail, saying they fear for their safety and for witnesses. The plea will be heard on Nov 20.Through advocate Prince Kumar Upadhyay, Lohar's father, Ramesh Lohar, filed an intervention plea describing the attack as a cruel, unprovoked murder."A young man of 22 was killed in a public train over a trivial quarrel. His parents have lost their son," the reply said, adding that releasing Suvarna would prejudice the prosecution and erode public confidence in commuter safety. The incident occurred late on June 23, 2026, on a Nalasopara-bound fast local from Andheri.Police said Lohar was returning from work when a dispute began near the door after rainwater splashed into the compartment.Passengers separated the men. After the alarm chain was pulled between Goregaon and Malad, the assailant allegedly stabbed Lohar in the chest and abdomen. He was taken to Shatabdi Hospital, where he was declared dead before admission.The family's reply says Lohar was unarmed and had not assaulted anyone. It alleges that, about eight minutes after passengers intervened, Suvarna walked to Lohar's new position, took a knife from his bag and stabbed him multiple times on vital parts, then threatened passengers before fleeing.The defence says Suvarna and Lohar were strangers, there was no motive or premeditation, no weapon was recovered from Suvarna, and CCTV did not show the stabbing. It also questioned the test identification parade.The family says Suvarna was traced through technical evidence, a doctor linked the injuries to the weapon, and the knife seller identified him. articles.title: Marriage and motherhood should not affect career: Karnataka high court
articles.summary: BENGALURU: Marriage, motherhood and raising children should not affect a woman's professional career or tie her down to one place, Karnataka high court
articles.body: BENGALURU: Marriage, motherhood and raising children should not affect a woman's professional career or tie her down to one place, Karnataka high court has observed in a recent judgement, clearing an ophthalmologist's relocation to the United Kingdom.In an order passed on Oct 29, Justice Lalitha Kanneganti disposed of a petition filed by the woman's husband, who resides in Mumbai. He had challenged the order of a Bengaluru family court that directed him to deliver the original passport of their minor child to his wife and provide consent to obtain a visa to travel to the United Kingdom.He had challenged another order rejecting his request for a change in interim custody of the minor child from the wife's family to his family, along with other consequential relief.'Motherhood doesn't confine a woman to single place'The wife argued she had been taking care of the child since 2019 when they were thrown out of their residence in Mumbai. According to her, employment in the UK provides a better and more secure financial position, enabling her to provide the child with stable housing, education, healthcare and extracurricular opportunities."Marriage and motherhood do not require her to remain confined to a particular place," the judge said, specifying conditions for mutual visits: The mother shall allow regular audio and video calls between the father and the child at least for 20 minutes a day; the father shall get parenting time with the child during school holidays; twice in a year during the child's holidays, the mother shall send the boy to India to spend 75% of the vacation with the father; the father could go to the United Kingdom to meet the child for 75% of the holidays.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Bengaluru | Silver Rate in Bengaluru | Bank Holidays in Bengaluru | Public Holidays in Bengaluru | Bengaluru AQI | Weather in Bengaluru | Petrol Price in Bengaluru | Diesel Price in Bengaluru | CNG Price in Bengaluru | LPG Price in BengaluruStay updated with the latest Bengaluru news. articles.title: Research claims that many companies in the US are calling back employees they fired and replaced by AI; and it is costing them more, as sacked employees now …
articles.summary: Nearly one in five US workers say they have experienced a surprising workplace reversal: their employer replaced them with artificial intelligence (AI),
articles.body: Nearly one in five US workers say they have experienced a surprising workplace reversal: their employer replaced them with artificial intelligence (AI), only to ask them to come back later, a report has found. According to new research from talent assessment firm SHL, this growing trend – which the firm calls “AI rebounding” – suggests several companies are learning the hard way that AI cannot do everything human employees can. And bringing those workers back is proving expensive.The SHL survey, conducted in June and July, and published recently, found that 19.1% of US respondents had been replaced by AI and subsequently asked to return to their jobs. Across both the US and the UK, that figure stood at 16%. However, those returning workers are not coming back on the old terms.According to SHL:51% demanded a substantial pay increase before agreeing to return.42% required written guarantees about their future job security.40% wanted clear transparency on how AI would be used in their roles.“Organisations are making fast, sometimes myopic, decisions about their people based on an incomplete picture of what their employees can do with or without AI. AI rebounding is what happens when a company automates a role before it has genuinely assessed the human capability inside it. The AI doesn’t deliver, the gap becomes obvious, and the business ends up rehiring the same experts they just let go of, at a far greater cost,” said Lucy Beaumont, global senior vice president of product and design at SHL, in a press release.Areas where companies are finding AI falls shortSHL’s findings line up with a separate July survey from Robert Half. That study found that 32% of US hiring managers whose companies cut jobs because of AI eventually had to bring back the same or similar positions. Among those hiring managers, the gaps left by automation were clear:40% said the roles required institutional knowledge or context that AI could not replicate.39% cited relationship management.39% pointed to increased business demand.38% said the jobs needed more human oversight and quality control than the company expected.Klarna and Ford adjust courseSeveral major companies have already run into these limits firsthand. For example, Swedish buy-now, pay-later firm Klarna recently began hiring human customer service representatives again after leaning heavily on AI chatbots.CEO Sebastian Siemiatkowski acknowledged the company had gone too far with automation, Bloomberg reported. A Klarna spokesperson told Fortune that human agents were necessary “for complex, sensitive cases,” noting the company was directly hiring a “small number” of high-skilled workers to see where the “human touch” adds the most value.Similarly, automaker Ford made a move in June, hiring and promoting 350 experienced engineers after AI-powered quality control tools fell short of expectations. While Ford noted that AI has helped improve quality, a company representative told Fortune that “these engineers carry the hard-earned wisdom of decades of design,” adding that pairing AI with deep technical expertise is what actually gets results.AI layoffs continue to climbEven as some employers backtrack, overall AI-driven job cuts are still rising sharply.As per the data from outplacement firm Challenger, Gray & Christmas, employers cited AI in 121,401 announced job cuts through October. That is already more than double the 54,836 AI-related layoffs announced during all of 2025. The report also said younger workers are taking the brunt of the shift. A study from the Stanford Digital Economy Lab found that employment among workers aged 22 to 25 in jobs heavily exposed to AI was 19% lower than it would have been if it had grown at the same pace as less-exposed fields.You use AI every day. articles.title: Charlie Kirk murder trial set for June 2028 as judge rejects defence's push for 2029
articles.summary: The trial of the man accused of assassinating conservative activist Charlie Kirk will begin in June 2028, a Utah judge ruled on Monday, setting a schedule
articles.body: The trial of the man accused of assassinating conservative activist Charlie Kirk will begin in June 2028, a Utah judge ruled on Monday, setting a schedule that falls between the timelines proposed by prosecutors and the defence.Tyler Robinson, 23, has pleaded not guilty to aggravated murder charge. Kirk, 31, was shot dead while addressing thousands of people at Utah Valley University. Robinson could face the death penalty if convicted, AP reported.District Judge Tony Graf allotted 105 days for the proceedings, with jury selection scheduled to begin on June 21, 2028. Robinson's lawyers had proposed starting the trial in 2029, while prosecutors said they could be ready by October 2027 and had suggested January 2028 to avoid the Thanksgiving and Christmas holidays.Graf said the schedule sought to balance Robinson's right to prepare his defence with Kirk's widow Erika Kirk's right to a speedy resolution.Kirk family expresses disappointment over trial dateErika Kirk's attorney, Jeffrey Neiman, disagreed with the timeline, saying the family had wanted the trial to begin as early as next October.“A trial in the summer of 2028, three years after Charlie's assassination, does not feel very speedy to the Kirk family,” Neiman told the judge.The Kirk family described the decision as a “delay” in a statement issued after the hearing, saying, “every additional day without justice prolongs our family's pain.”The case has drawn attention from Kirk's supporters, including US President Donald Trump, who called for a swift trial in a social media post last month. Trump said Robinson should be tried “within a month” and criticised Graf for “taking forever to ask questions that people already know the answer to.”Kirk had helped mobilise young voters in support of Trump during the 2024 presidential election.What are the charges against Robinson?Prosecutors allege that Robinson targeted Kirk because of his political beliefs. They have said a bullet recovered from the rifle allegedly used in the killing was engraved with the words “Hey Facist! CATCH!”They have also cited a text message allegedly written by Robinson about Kirk: “I had enough of his hatred. Some hate can't be negotiated out.”Robinson turned himself in a day after the shooting. His lawyers have not presented an alternative account of Kirk's killing.Defence seeks more time to prepare caseRobinson's attorneys have argued that they need to examine tens of thousands of files provided by prosecutors. They also plan to investigate his background extensively to identify mitigating factors that could affect his sentence if he is convicted.The defence has further said it will conduct surveys to assess whether an impartial jury can be selected in Utah County. Depending on the findings, it may seek to move the trial to another location.Graf said he would hear arguments over the trial venue next December.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Sundar Pichai sends welcome note to Mark Zuckerberg; says: Excited to serve our Google's …
articles.summary: Mark Zuckerberg recently shared a post on X announcing that Meta's Muse Ember, Muse Spark 1.3, and Muse Wonder are now accessible via Google Cloud's Model
articles.body: Mark Zuckerberg recently shared a post on X announcing that Meta's Muse Ember, Muse Spark 1.3, and Muse Wonder are now accessible via Google Cloud's Model Garden managed APIs. The models are multimodal with 1M token context windows; Ember stands out as Meta's smallest and cheapest option, delivering intelligence comparable to models like Claude Haiku at roughly one-third the per-task cost for sub-agent and repetitive work. Google CEO Sundar Pichai replied to the Meta CEO welcoming the models, highlighting cross-company collaboration where Google Cloud hosts and serves Meta's proprietary AI to enterprise customers alongside its own Gemini offerings.“Muse Ember, Muse Spark 1.3, and Muse Wonder are now available on Google Cloud,” Mark Zuckerberg wrote in the post. “Congrats and welcome to the model garden, excited to serve our Google Cloud customers!,” Sundar Pichai replied.What is Muse WonderMuse Wonder is claimed to be Meta’s most capable frontier model, purpose-built for complex software engineering, offering an optimal balance of speed, reliability, and deep persistence. Muse Wonder offers native computer use and long-context understanding, enabling the execution of sophisticated, multi-step workflows across browsers, desktop, and mobile applications. Muse Wonder models offer state-of-the-art coding, orchestration, and multimodal reasoning capabilities, and feature sub-agent delegation, parallel tool calling, and agentic memory.Top use cases include real-world software engineering, multi-file repository updates, and end-to-end workflow automation. It can also operate everyday applications, support complex legal and professional knowledge work, and reason over vast codebases.What is Muse Spark 1.3Muse Spark 1.3, available on Google Cloud, is a workhorse agentic model designed for long-horizon workflows, offering an optimal balance of intelligence, speed, and scalable performance. Muse Spark 1.3 offers native tool calling and MCP server integration, enabling the creation of sophisticated AI agents that complete multi-step tasks across professional and personal workflows. articles.summary: NEW DELHI: A 60-year-old bus driver was burnt to death after unidentified miscreants set fire to a parked bus in Bangladesh's Faridpur early Monday, as a
articles.body: NEW DELHI: A 60-year-old bus driver was burnt to death after unidentified miscreants set fire to a parked bus in Bangladesh's Faridpur early Monday, as a series of arson attacks and crude bomb explosions were reported in Dhaka and several other districts.The deceased, identified as Md Kalachan Sheikh, was sleeping inside a bus belonging to Kishore-Tanay Paribahan near Goalchamat New Bus Stand when it was set on fire, reported Bangladesh Daily New Age (Bangladesh). Firefighters rescued him and took him to Faridpur Medical College Hospital, where doctors declared him dead.In another incident, a petrol bomb was hurled at a double-decker bus carrying around 35 students of Islamic University in Jhenaidah on Monday night. The bus, named Diganta, was travelling towards the university campus when the attack took place in the Dragon Bagan area of Shailkupa upazila. No casualties were reported.In Dhaka, at least two crude bombs exploded in front of Tokyo Square in the Mohammadpur area around 9:15pm on Monday. Police said they were yet to identify those responsible.Separately, a Basumati Paribahan bus was set on fire in front of the Mirpur-11 Post Office around 9.30pm. No one was injured.In Bogura district, a van carrying jute sacks was set on fire on the Dhaka-Bogura highway in Sherpur upazila on Monday evening. The vehicle was gutted, temporarily disrupting traffic. Firefighters brought the blaze under control.More buses torched in Dhaka, Savar and GazipurThe incidents came amid a wider spate of arson attacks and crude bomb explosions across Bangladesh. According to The Daily Star, six buses were set on fire in Savar, Dhaka and Gazipur on Monday.In Savar, two buses parked along the Dhaka-Aricha highway were torched in the Genda and Baliarpur areas around 1am and 4am, respectively. One was used to transport garment workers, while the other belonged to Itihash Paribahan. The fires damaged the buses' seats and interiors.In Dhaka, a Lovely Paribahan bus was set on fire beneath the Farmgate metro station in the evening. Another bus, belonging to Basumati Paribahan, was torched under the metro rail line in Mirpur-11 around 9:15pm.In Gazipur's Kaliakair upazila, two parked buses were set on fire in the Chandra area along the Dhaka-Tangail highway, The Daily Star reported.Crude bomb explosions were also reported from several parts of Dhaka, including Banasree, Mohakhali, Dhaka University campus and outside the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Court.Police step up security, arrest 19Amid the attacks, the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) set up 160 additional checkpoints at key locations across the capital on Monday and deployed more personnel to prevent further incidents.DMP Deputy Commissioner (Media) Akhter Hossain told The Daily Star that police had arrested at least 19 people in the preceding 24 hours in connection with recent blasts and attacks. He said many of those arrested were linked to the Awami League, whose activities are currently banned, reported The Daily Star.Police in Savar also suspected the involvement of the banned Awami League in the two bus arson incidents there. Investigations were under way to identify those responsible.The attacks come amid heightened political tensions in Bangladesh following the July 2024 uprising that led to the ouster of former prime minister Sheikh Hasina. The Awami League's activities were subsequently banned, and authorities have alleged links of some of its leaders and activists to recent incidents of crude bomb explosions and vehicle arson.You use AI every day. articles.title: After Ivan wrecked his Alabama timber, Salem Saloom planted tougher longleaf pines; two decades later, 1,100 acres shelter gopher tortoises
articles.summary: Discover how Salem Saloom transformed his hurricane-damaged Alabama timberland into a thriving ecosystem with longleaf pines, providing a habitat for gopher tortoises and contributing to climate change initiatives.
articles.body: Imagine spending 20 years building something up, and then one storm wipes out a large part of it. That's what happened to Salem Saloom in 2004. According to The Nature Conservancy, Dr Salem Saloom, a semi-retired physician and priest-in-training, when the group profiled him in 2024, lost about $250,000 worth of timber on his farm to Hurricane Ivan. Rather than giving up, he saw an opportunity to start over with a tougher tree. Two decades later, that tree covers about 1,100 acres of his land and gopher tortoises live there.Haunting retreat that grew into a tree farm Saloom’s story goes back to 1983, when he purchased 160 acres of land in Evergreen, Alabama, to hunt and take time off from a surgery practice. The land had previously been used for the production of peanuts and corn. Along with his young son Patrick, he started planting pine trees to reduce soil erosion and help prevent flooding. Over the next 15 years, along with his wife, Dianne, he bought about 2,000 additional acres of land. Saloom also learned how to conduct prescribed burns. By 2010, the farm had been named the Family Tree Farm of the Year at the regional, state, and national levels.A stone, then smarter choice Ivan hit the Gulf Coast as a Category 3 storm in 2004. Saloom’s town is more than 90 miles from where it made landfall, yet the damage was severe. The storm destroyed about a quarter million dollars' worth of timber, most of it being fast-growing loblolly pine. It took five months to remove the wreckage. Saloom said they decided to “make lemonade out of lemons.” Saloom chose longleaf pine. It is a native tree and more storm-tolerant than loblolly. It also grows slower. That's why loblolly was planted so widely as demand for wood increased. Saloom turned to the Natural Resources Conservation Service, a US Department of Agriculture agency, for help. It runs the Farm Bill-funded Environmental Quality Incentive Program, or EQIP. In 2006, he got the funding and technical assistance and planted 154 acres of longleaf that year. Since then, he has planted about 1,100 acres.What the research saysIn a 2009 article published in the Southern Journal of Applied Forestry, Kurt Johnsen and colleagues examined three pine species in southeast Mississippi after Hurricane Katrina in 2005. Only 7% of the longleaf pine trees died from wind damage. For the loblolly pine, the figure was 26%. Slash pine fell in between at 14%, and only the gap between longleaf and loblolly was statistically significant. The authors’ conclusion was that longleaf pine is more resistant to wind damage compared to loblolly. This is a single study and cannot be treated as the last word. However, it does support Saloom’s choice, since most of the trees Ivan knocked down on his farm were loblolly.Then there are the tortoises. The white sticks scattered across Saloom’s farm mark gopher tortoise burrows. A 2004 paper, ‘Habitat Associations of Gopher Tortoise Burrows on Industrial Timberlands,’ looked at where they dig. In 1994, Jeanne Jones and Brian Dorr surveyed timberlands in Southern Mississippi and Southwestern Alabama, finding 460 active burrows. Active burrows are more common in deep sandy soils and in sites with open tree cover. The authors theorised that by restoring longleaf pine on sandy ridges, good tortoise habitat could be created. They recommended things such as prescribed fire, midstory control and thinning. Saloom's farm was not part of the study, but the theory and advice matched with his farm and his methods.What he left behind In 2024, The Nature Conservancy reported that his newest parcel included an old cemetery with headstones dating to the 18th century. He planned to clear the overgrown land, replant it and sign it up for a USDA carbon credit program. Saloom believed that well-managed family forests could help in the fight against climate change. He imagined a naturally regenerated longleaf forest, like the ones that had flourished there for thousands of years. “It's never been work for me,” he said. “It goes beyond work.” Saloom died on 29 July 2026, aged 78. The forest he left behind will continue his legacy.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: To ease food shortages, the US imported 1,250 reindeer from Siberia to Alaska; herd estimates hit 600,000 by 1932, then plunged to about 25,000 by 1950
articles.summary: Discover the fascinating history of reindeer in Alaska, from their introduction in the 1890s to the dramatic decline of the herd size by 1950, influenced by environmental factors and government policies.
articles.body: Reindeer are so tied to Christmas in the public mind that it is easy to forget they once carried a serious government mission in Alaska. In the 1890s, Washington shipped them over from Siberia to feed a hungry region and for a few decades, the plan looked like a runaway success. Then the herds fell apart, almost as quickly as they had grown.Jackson’s 1891 plan for Northwestern AlaskaReindeer first reached Alaska near Teller, on the Seward Peninsula, in 1891, brought by Reverend Sheldon Jackson. The Alaska Department of Fish and Game (ADF&G) states that roughly 1,280 Siberian reindeer were introduced between 1892 and 1902 and that Sámi herders were brought over to teach herding to Alaska Natives. The need for it was genuine. The department also reports that caribou were rare in northwest Alaska, moose were non-existent and commercial hunting had already reduced the number of bowhead whales and walruses. Jackson viewed reindeer as a dependable supply of red meat and an opportunity for Alaska Natives to join the cash economy.Herds passed 600,000 by 1932 The National Park Service article on Frank Churchill’s 1905 Documentation of the Reindeer Service in Alaska noted that ownership became complicated, since missionary organisations controlled large herds even as the government tried to promote ownership among Alaska Native communities. ADF&G found that the Sámi herder and the missionary churches derived more benefits from the industry before the 1920s than the Alaska Natives did. Whites took over the business by the 1920s. Herbert C. Hanson’s Importance and Development of the Reindeer Industry in Alaska, published in the Journal of Range Management, reports that numbers rose steadily to over 600,000 by 1932.Jim Dau’s Managing reindeer and wildlife on Alaska’s Seward Peninsula, published in Polar Research in 2000, looks at that last pressure more closely. According to Dau, when the reindeer was introduced during the period 1892-1902, no other ungulate animal was present, while the population of big carnivores was lower than what it would later be. He further claims that the caribou affected the Seward Peninsula reindeer industry, more than any other wildlife animal because reindeer intermingle with the caribou herds and stray from their allotted range and through competition over the food. Hanson’s report also tracked herd size from 1892-1951.The paper says the reindeer industry then became part of a much broader landscape change. Over the century that followed, herd numbers and range grew and then fell sharply, with most of the drop coming between 1932 and 1950; while wildlife spread across the Seward Peninsula through natural movement and translocations. Dau also notes that the industry was hit hardest by wildlife, especially caribou and that cooperative management efforts later tried to blend indigenous, scientific and local knowledge with government programmes.The Reindeer Act of 1937 and what followed ADF&G described how the Great Depression had led to the collapse of the market for reindeer meat in the rest of the USA while the local demands did not match the supply. Dealings with non-Native businessmen drove local Alaska Native herders to despair, ADF&G’s Reindeer: Vehicles of Change said. Herding practices declined and animals started wandering.In 1937, Congress passed the Reindeer Act, which effectively limited reindeer ownership in Alaska to Alaska Natives, according to Title 25 of the US Code. In 1940, the federal government purchased the reindeer owned by non-Natives and gave them to Native herders. Vehicles of Change put the population at around 25,000 by 1950, after the fall and it held at roughly 25,000-30,000 from there, with most herds on the Seward Peninsula. By 1950, the account was down to about 25,000, a fraction of the 1932 peak of more than 600,000. The animals stayed on the Seward Peninsula and after the 1940 federal buyout, the herds were in the hands of Alaska Native herders, not the missionary groups and non-Native operators who had run the business before. It was a small, quiet industry next to what Jackson had pictured in the 1890s.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: India, Oman begin naval exercise as Arabian Sea security takes centre stage
articles.summary: A large share of India's crude oil imports and exports passes through the Arabian Sea and the western Indian Ocean.
articles.body: A large share of India's crude oil imports and exports passes through the Arabian Sea and the western Indian Ocean. Any disruption in these waters can quickly affect freight rates, insurance costs and supply chains.Against this backdrop, Indian Naval Ship (INS) Surat arrived in Muscat, Oman, on November 8 to participate in the 15th edition of the bilateral maritime exercise Naseem Al Bahr, followed by a Coordinated Patrol (CORPAT) with the Royal Navy of Oman.The exercise includes harbour and sea phases, with cross-deck visits, operational interactions and sporting events. The aim is to allow personnel from both navies to exchange operational experience and best practices, improve interoperability and strengthen mutual understanding.The port call is in line with the government's MAHASAGAR vision, short for Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions. It also builds on the 13th meeting of the India-Oman Joint Military Cooperation Committee, held on November 24, 2025.Press Information Bureau+1Why these waters matterThe western maritime approaches connect India's ports with the Gulf, the Red Sea, Europe and the east coast of Africa. The Gulf of Aden and the waters off Somalia are particularly important because they provide access to the Red Sea and the Suez Canal, a major shipping route between Asia and Europe. Any disruption caused by conflict, piracy or attacks on merchant vessels can affect India's energy security and export industries.The Indian Navy has maintained an anti-piracy deployment in the Gulf of Aden since 2008. In July 2026, INS Trikand responded to an attempted pirate attack on the merchant vessel MV Golden Arsenal, approximately 300 nautical miles (550 km) east-northeast of Djibouti. The warship deployed a boarding team, supported by a P-8I maritime patrol aircraft, to secure the vessel and assess the situation.In 2026, the Navy also launched Operation Urja Suraksha to protect merchant shipping and India's energy interests amid the worsening security situation in West Asia.Its role extends beyond anti-piracy patrols. INS Tarkash, deployed in the western Indian Ocean from January 2025, supported Combined Task Force 150 of the 47-nation Combined Maritime Forces (CMF). On March 31, 2025, the warship intercepted a vessel carrying more than 2,500 kg of narcotics.On October 14, 2026, the Indian Navy relinquished command of Combined Task Force 154, the CMF's maritime training task force, at a ceremony in Bahrain. During its eight-month command, the Navy oversaw multinational training and capacity-building initiatives involving personnel from 39 countries.Working with partners in the regionINS Trikand visited Maputo, Mozambique, in March 2026, where it conducted joint training with the Mozambique Navy. On departure, the warship also undertook joint surveillance of Mozambique's exclusive economic zone, with Mozambican naval personnel on board.INS Sunayna's deployments under the IOS SAGAR initiative in 2025 and 2026 further demonstrated India's efforts to strengthen regional maritime cooperation. The 2025 mission included 44 naval personnel from nine partner countries, while the 2026 deployment brought together 38 personnel from 16 partner nations for multinational training and operational engagements across the Indian Ocean region.The Navy's operational reach was on display again on November 2, when INS Kolkata, supported by Indian Air Force assets, helped rescue all 20 crew members of the Iranian fishing vessel Azini, which had been hijacked by armed pirates off Somalia.The operation, conducted over 48 hours more than 3,000 km from Mumbai, involved maritime surveillance, marine commandos and an IAF C-17 aircraft that airdropped additional personnel. The crew was rescued without casualties.

articles.summary: US President Donald Trump has said he does not recall reading a memo in which secretary of state Marco Rubio flagged Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's
articles.body: US President Donald Trump has said he does not recall reading a memo in which secretary of state Marco Rubio flagged Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with an alleged Chinese spy.Speaking to reporters at the White House, Trump said the intelligence warning may have been mentioned to him but did not make much of an impact. He said, "I would certainly check with the intelligence people. It could have been mentioned. Certainly, it didn't make much of an impact on me."This comes as the FBI investigates Huang's association with the accused Chinese operative, Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le.Despite the allegations, Trump continued to defend the Nvidia chief, saying he had personally questioned him about his association with Alice Huang."He said, 'I had no idea she was a spy', and I really believe him," Trump told reporters.The US President also said he expected Huang to be in a good position as the FBI examined the matter."I know the FBI is looking into it in terms of something else, and I think that he'll be in good shape," Trump said.Trump had earlier expressed confidence in the tech executive, describing him as "an honourable guy" and saying he "probably has an excuse for it". When asked on Sunday whether he regretted not acting on the allegations earlier, the President said he had no remorse.Also Read|Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang loses $7.4bn in 30 minutes, drops 2 spots in Forbes rich listRubio flagged Huang's links before Trump's China visitThe New York Times reported that Rubio had flagged Jensen Huang's relationship with the alleged Chinese operative in a memo circulated ahead of Trump's visit to Beijing in May.The disclosure adds to questions over when the US administration became aware of the alleged connection and what action it considered taking.The latest revelation follows an earlier report by The New York Times that Trump had been briefed nearly a year ago that US intelligence agencies had electronically surveilled Alice Huang over suspicions that she was spying for Beijing.Initially, surveillance established her association with an unidentified American national. Intelligence officials later identified the individual as Jensen Huang.According to the earlier report, Trump chose not to take punitive action at the time. He reportedly considered Nvidia's advanced chips important to America's competition with China in artificial intelligence. He also viewed the company's market value as important to supporting financial markets.FBI investigates Alice's association with Chinese operativeAlice Huang, who is not related to Jensen Huang, previously served as managing director of Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company that had commercial partnerships with Nvidia.The allegations have raised national security concerns in Washington, particularly over the possible transfer of sensitive intellectual property involving Nvidia's advanced artificial intelligence processors.The FBI is examining Jensen Huang's association with the accused operative. Nvidia has also initiated an independent internal inquiry into the matter.The controversy has triggered international scrutiny over the Nvidia chief's alleged involvement. Huang has publicly acknowledged the relationship and apologised to his spouse.Huang's lobbying for China chip sales under scrutinyThe allegations have emerged as Jensen Huang continues to lobby Washington for relaxed export controls on Nvidia's semiconductor shipments to mainland China.Trump has authorised Nvidia to supply its H200 artificial intelligence chips to Beijing over the course of the year. However, it remains unclear whether Chinese regulators will allow domestic companies to purchase the processors in significant volumes.The controversy has also drawn attention to the strategic importance of Nvidia's technology in the US-China artificial intelligence race.China has rejected the espionage allegations, describing them as part of a coordinated smear campaign against Beijing.You use AI every day. articles.title: Six journalists killed, 33 years of defiance: Russia's last major independent newspaper shuts down
articles.summary: Russia's last major independent newspaper critical of the Kremlin, Novaya Gazeta, shut down its Moscow office on Monday after three decades, citing
articles.body: Russia's last major independent newspaper critical of the Kremlin, Novaya Gazeta, shut down its Moscow office on Monday after three decades, citing sustained pressure from government officials and security agencies.The newspaper, which has faced mounting restrictions since Russia launched its invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, said authorities had forced its editorial team to cease operations.In a statement published on October 30, the newspaper said Russian authorities and security services had "forced our editorial team to cease operations.”“Human rights and freedoms have been abolished in this country, and defending them is now treated as a crime,” the newspaper said, "Elections and elected governing bodies have been effectively dismantled, civil society institutions have been wiped out, freedom of conscience and human dignity have been trampled underfoot.”On Monday, journalists cleared the Moscow office, slowly taking down portraits of six colleagues who were killed for their work. The photographs had hung in the newsroom where reporters and editors once planned their investigations.As staff gathered outside the building, a new sign was placed above the newspaper's former nameplate. It read, “Here lived Novaya Gazeta.”Tatiana Britskaya, the editor of Novaya Gazeta's investigations desk, said she had expected the newspaper to shut down almost every day over the past four-and-a-half years.“It is an incredibly difficult decision, because this is more than a workplace, more than an office -- this is our home, and we're losing it,” she said.Sergei Sokolov, the newspaper's editor-in-chief, expressed hope that it would eventually return.“We will live, and I am sure that this country, caught in such a terrible era, will eventually stir. As soon as those first signs appear, Novaya Gazeta will return, to our readers and to our colleagues.”Crackdown on independent mediaFounded in 1993, Novaya Gazeta earned a reputation for investigative journalism, particularly its reporting on human rights violations and corruption in Russia. Six of its journalists have been killed, including Anna Politkovskaya, who reported on atrocities during the second Chechen War.Politkovskaya was shot dead in her apartment building in 2006, during Vladimir Putin's first term as president.The newspaper faced increasing government pressure as the Kremlin tightened its grip on critics. The crackdown intensified after Russia invaded Ukraine in February 2022, forcing several independent media organisations to close or move their operations abroad.Novaya Gazeta was fined over allegations that it had discredited Russia's armed forces. Authorities also designated it a “foreign agent”, a label that carries strong negative connotations and exposes those named to additional government scrutiny.Its online platforms were blocked, its printing house was seized, its media registration was revoked and its reader donation system was shut down. The latest order to vacate its Moscow office marked another blow to the publication.Longtime editor-in-chief Dmitry Muratov, who shared the 2021 Nobel Peace Prize with Philippine journalist Maria Ressa, also faced intimidation. In 2022, an attacker poured red paint over him on a train, causing severe irritation in his eyes. Muratov stepped down as editor in 2023 after being designated a “foreign agent”.Some of the newspaper's journalists left Russia in 2022 and established a separate publication, Novaya Gazeta Europe. The outlet continues to criticise the Kremlin and its military campaign in Ukraine.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Russia hits Black Sea vessels, Ukraine targets power supply as peace talks loom
articles.summary: Russia and Ukraine continued to exchange strikes on Tuesday, targeting vessels and infrastructure, as officials from the two countries and the United
articles.body: Russia and Ukraine continued to exchange strikes on Tuesday, targeting vessels and infrastructure, as officials from the two countries and the United States prepared to hold their first trilateral peace talks in Abu Dhabi.The Russian defence ministry said its forces had struck a cargo vessel and a tanker in the Black Sea, Interfax news agency reported. Another cargo vessel was hit east of the Ukrainian port of Odesa, the agency said.Meanwhile, a Ukrainian drone attack disrupted power supplies in Luhansk and other parts of the eastern region controlled by Russia, TASS reported, quoting Moscow-installed authorities. Reuters said it could not immediately independently verify the report.In a separate incident, a drone struck an industrial facility in the central Ukrainian city of Kremenchuk, a Ukrainian official said in a post on Telegram. The official did not provide further details.Russia and Ukraine have regularly targeted each other's energy infrastructure and other assets since Moscow launched its full-scale invasion in February 2022.Russia, Ukraine show flexibility over eastern regions: US officialsThe latest exchanges came as senior officials from Russia, Ukraine and the US prepared to meet in Abu Dhabi for the first trilateral negotiations aimed at ending the conflict since February. The talks are taking place as the fifth anniversary of Russia's full-scale invasion approaches.US officials said Moscow and Kyiv had privately demonstrated “a little bit of flexibility” over the question of control of Ukraine's eastern territories in a postwar arrangement, BBC reported.However, the two sides remain divided over the terms for ending the war. One of the main points of disagreement is the eastern region of Donetsk, most of which is currently occupied by Russia.Moscow has demanded that Ukraine surrender the parts of Donetsk that remain under Kyiv's control. Ukraine, meanwhile, wants to freeze the current line of contact, retaining control over the territory it still holds and describing it as vital to its future security.Talks to address postwar securityUS President Donald Trump's son-in-law and a member of the American delegation, Jared Kushner, alongside peace envoy Steve Witkoff, said the discussions would focus on the postwar security concerns of both countries.“An important part of this process is encouraging all parties to begin thinking seriously about what comes after the war,” Kushner wrote on X.Despite the reported flexibility over territorial arrangements, the positions of Moscow and Kyiv on the conditions for ending the conflict remain far apart.You use AI every day. articles.title: Netanyahu's daily calls to Trump over Iran war spark pushback within White House: Report
articles.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has been calling US President Donald Trump every day to urge him to resume military action against Iran, even as
articles.body: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has been calling US President Donald Trump every day to urge him to resume military action against Iran, even as Arab and Muslim leaders along with officials in White House step up efforts to prevent a fresh escalation and push Washington towards negotiations."Netanyahu calls him every day [to urge him to resume the war]. Those who don't want a war within the White House and outside have been trying to combat that," a person briefed on the discussions told the Financial Times.The person said regional leaders were urging Trump not to escalate the conflict and to prioritise negotiations. At least four Arab and Muslim leaders have spoken to the US president in recent days, seeking to persuade him to give diplomacy more time amid concerns that Washington could launch fresh strikes after last week's midterm elections.The leaders include Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, Qatar's Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani and Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan.Their efforts come as Trump has signalled that renewed US military action against Iran is unlikely for now, saying there is "positive momentum" towards ending the conflict.Trump made the remarks after meeting Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani at the White House on Monday. Vice-President JD Vance also attended the meeting. Qatar has been spearheading regional efforts to broker an interim agreement between Washington and Tehran.A diplomat briefed on the discussions described the meeting as "positive", saying there was agreement that diplomacy was the preferred way forward to reach a deal.Trump says Iran war is 'effectively over'Trump said Iran was militarily "effectively over" and indicated that a fresh US attack was not necessary at this stage. He nevertheless said American forces remained prepared to act if circumstances changed.In a post on Truth Social, Trump said there was "positive momentum toward an end to this Conflict", adding that the US would continue to protect its interests.He also said Qatar, Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Bahrain, Kuwait and other countries preferred the status quo, including the continuation of the US naval blockade of Iran.Trump's remarks come amid uncertainty over whether he would order fresh strikes after the midterm elections. The war and its impact on fuel prices were among the key issues for US voters, with Republicans suffering major losses in the polls.Although, Arab and Muslim leaders are concerned that renewed military action could plunge the region into a deeper crisis and trigger a strong Iranian response against neighbouring countries.Anwar Gargash, diplomatic adviser to the UAE president, said the priority should remain diplomatic efforts. "The priority must remain the pursuit of political diplomatic solutions capable of producing a more sustainable regional balance," he said.Gargash added that it was perhaps too early to assess the impact of the US midterm election results on Washington's approach towards Iran, but expressed hope that they would reinforce efforts to pursue diplomatic solutions and ensure stability in the Gulf.Iran, meanwhile, has warned that it is prepared to respond to any fresh attacks. It has also threatened to target undersea cables in the Strait of Hormuz and data centres in the region, raising concerns that any renewed confrontation could spread beyond the immediate conflict zone.The diplomatic push comes as mediators have struggled for weeks to break a deadlock between Washington and Tehran over an interim agreement.Both sides have been working with mediators on a proposal based on a version of a seven-day plan presented by Iran in September. Trump had rejected the proposal.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.body: Russia expects the main focus of fresh peace talks on Ukraine, scheduled to begin in Abu Dhabi later on Tuesday, to be discussions on establishing a new post-war security framework for Europe, a source in the Russian delegation said.Russian and Ukrainian officials are set to hold two days of US-mediated negotiations, their first meeting since February. The talks come after US President Donald Trump said last week that a broader peace agreement could be within reach, potentially addressing Europe's security concerns as well.A source in the Russian delegation told news agency Reuters, the discussions would centre on developing mechanisms to prevent security threats and enhance regional stability."While a settlement in Ukraine remains a matter of critical importance, it is only one part of these broader discussions and is subordinate to the main objective of establishing a comprehensive and indivisible security architecture for the entire continent," the source said.Representatives from France, Britain, Germany, the European union, NATO and Italy are also expected to be in Abu Dhabi, where they are likely to hold discussions with US and Ukrainian officials. Moscow, however, has not indicated whether it will engage in any direct discussions with European representatives during the week.Russia's 11-member delegation is being led by presidential aide Vladimir Medinsky. articles.body: Boeing said it plans to reduce about 5% of its commercial airplane workforce through a combination of attrition and layoffs, as the aerospace giant grapples with a slower-than-expected production ramp-up across its jet programmes. According to a report by CNBC, in a memo to employees on Monday, Stephanie Pope, head of Boeing Commercial Airplanes, said the company needs to align staffing levels with revised production plans after adjusting its manufacturing schedules and lowering aircraft output targets. “Adjusting our production schedules and reducing aircraft output puts us in an overstaffed position,” Pope wrote in the note. “Unfortunately, that means we need to align our staffing levels to our revised business plan, resulting in a reduction of approximately 5% through a combination of attrition and involuntary layoffs, with notifications beginning in December.”Slower production growth behind workforce reductionThe planned cuts come as Boeing continues efforts to stabilise production of its bestselling 737 Max aircraft, manufactured near Seattle. The company had been working to increase output, but executives recently acknowledged that the production recovery is progressing more slowly than anticipated.Last month, Boeing CEO Kelly Ortberg told investors that the company does not expect a significant increase in 737 Max production until the second half of next year. He cited slower-than-expected wing production as one of the factors limiting the ramp-up. According to Pope, the mismatch between staffing levels and revised manufacturing plans has left the commercial aircraft division with more employees than required under current production forecasts.Boeing targets higher output by 2027Despite the job cuts, the CNBC report suggests that Boeing remains focused on increasing production rates over the longer term. The company is also targeting a production rate of 52 aircraft per month in the second half of 2027. Ortberg has previously said Boeing is presently working to stabilise output at roughly 47 Boeing 737 Max jets per month before pursuing a more aggressive production increase. The recent round of layoffs underscore the challenges Boeing is facing as it seeks to rebuild the manufacturing momentum while balancing costs and also adjusting to a slower recovery timeline. The company also revealed that the employee notifications about the job cuts will begin starting December.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: 'No real contact with him': Sonia Gandhi recalls face-to-face meetings with PM Modi in memoir
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Former Congress president Sonia Gandhi, in her memoir, has said that she has had \"practically no real contact\" with Prime Minister Narendra
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Former Congress president Sonia Gandhi, in her memoir, has said that she has had "practically no real contact" with Prime Minister Narendra Modi, despite his more than 12 years in office. She writes that PM Modi tends to look away and avoid eye contact when they come face-to-face.In her memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love, Sonia Gandhi said their interactions were largely limited to formal greetings at official gatherings and brief exchanges about her health.Describing their occasional encounters, Sonia said they usually meet at semi-official gatherings, such as the meetings of major political party leaders in the Speaker's chamber at the end of Parliament sessions."It's a very small room, and usually many people are present, but when he comes face-to-face with me, we greet each other with a formal namaste. This is different from the past, when leaders across party divides would treat one another with cordiality. He tends to look away, avoiding eye contact," she wrote.Sonia Gandhi recalled that PM Modi had occasionally enquired about her health after she returned from a hospital stay.He asked, "Theek hain aap?" to which she would reply, "Jee, ab main theek hoon, shukriya.""Apart from such brief exchanges, we have never really conversed, though we've exchanged formal birthday and New Year greetings over the years," she added.‘We come from different ideological worlds’Sonia Gandhi said her limited interaction with PM Modi was also set against a wider ideological divide between the two leaders. She described their political rivalry as a contest between contrasting visions of India, rather than a personal feud."We come from different ideological worlds; his idea of this country is vastly different from mine," she wrote.Explaining the difference, Sonia said, "All I learnt about India was assimilated from the members of my family, their lives of service, and their faith in a nation that encompassed a host of races and cultures, languages and faiths, based on principles of liberty and equality for all."On the contrary, she said PM Modi's vision of India was shaped by the RSS and his upbringing."Narendra Modi’s idea of India was constructed by the ideologues of the RSS and the experience of his own growing up. It affirmed a fundamentalism in which his faith and culture superseded all others. In that India, hierarchy, order, and control are central."Sonia said she stood for an India based on inclusiveness, secularism and social justice."He was fighting for his vision of India, and I for mine: an India against hegemony, an India that stands for inclusiveness, secularism, and social justice. It wasn't personal," she wrote.Sonia Gandhi on PM Modi's rise within the RSSSonia acknowledged that PM Modi had worked his way up within the RSS from an underprivileged background. However, she questioned the way his humble origins had been portrayed by his public relations team."Modi's origins may not have been as humble as his PR team has made out in marketing his image, but he had certainly worked his way to power within the RSS from an underprivileged world," she wrote.She also said PM Modi's political journey had been very different from hers. However, she found herself able to understand some of his discomfort with the ruling elite.Recalling her own experiences in Delhi's political circles, Sonia Gandhi said she often felt out of place during discussions in privileged drawing rooms. The views expressed there, she said, were far removed from the realities of ordinary Indians.She added that the suffering and struggle for survival she had witnessed in her constituency and during her travels across the country were unimaginable to this privileged group.‘Coarse language’ and attacks on opposition in ParliamentSonia Gandhi also criticised PM Modi's language in Parliament, alleging that he sometimes uses the same coarse language he employs at public rallies."When speaking in Parliament, he at times uses the same coarse language he employs in addressing a public rally. Much of the time he derides the opposition in what can only be termed a tirade," she wrote.She also accused the BJP of repeatedly targeting India's first prime minister, Jawaharlal Nehru, for establishing the country's democratic and secular foundations."Jawaharlal Nehru, our first prime minister, is a particular target of his party's hostility, for having set our country on a democratic and secular course," Sonia wrote.She further alleged that Sangh Parivar websites were filled with malicious abuse and falsehoods against Nehru.‘Congress-free India’: Sonia on BJP's opposition to CongressSonia Gandhi described the BJP's stated goal of a "Congress-free India" as an attempt to eliminate not just the party but also its policies and ideology.She said she believed the hostility towards Congress stemmed from the prime minister's conditioning by the RSS."I tend to believe that this antipathy stems from the conditioning of the prime minister by the RSS. It has inculcated in its cadre a commitment to an exclusionary, hardened version of Hinduism that has been crafted into a political agenda," she wrote.Sonia Gandhi recalls 2002 Gujarat riotsSonia Gandhi also revisited the 2002 Gujarat riots, which took place when PM Modi was the state's chief minister.Recalling the violence that followed the Godhra train tragedy, she said the Sabarmati Express was returning to Ahmedabad from Ayodhya with Hindu kar sevaks when four coaches caught fire. Fifty-nine pilgrims were killed. She noted that the cause of the fire remained disputed, while the communal violence that followed spread to several parts of Gujarat and claimed predominantly Muslim victims."When I was leader of the opposition in Parliament, I met the victims of many tragedies, and each time I was haunted by the misery I had witnessed," she wrote.She recalled watching television reports of the violence and trying to reach Congress colleagues in Gujarat who were seeking help."We watched the live reports in horror, and tried to get help to our colleagues in Gujarat who were calling us in desperation, but the administration failed to respond," she wrote.Sonia Gandhi said the riots were reported to have been fuelled by a fanatical fringe of the BJP and RSS, including the Bajrang Dal. PM Modi was the chief minister of Gujarat at the time.Sonia Gandhi on her understanding of Hinduism and faithSonia also contrasted the RSS's political interpretation of Hinduism with the inclusive understanding of faith she said she had learnt from her mother-in-law.She described this understanding as one that embraced different beliefs and paths, without being tied to a single deity, dogma, prophet or scripture."What I learnt from my mother-in-law is the faith that's been practised for centuries in India by vast numbers of our people -- from stalwarts of the freedom struggle to the poorest in our villages. It embraces diverse beliefs and different paths, adheres to no single deity, dogma, prophet, or scripture, and has included traditions of dissent," she wrote.She added that she had been educated in the principles of ahimsa and dharma as interpreted by Mahatma Gandhi. She also acknowledged the oppression and inequality associated with India's caste system, while pointing out that reformers had used ideas within Hinduism to challenge caste discrimination.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Must maintain political neutrality': EC says model code curbs apply to retired govt officials
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Election Commission on Tuesday extended the Model Code of Conduct (MCC) restrictions to retired state government officials engaged by state
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Election Commission on Tuesday extended the Model Code of Conduct (MCC) restrictions to retired state government officials engaged by state governments in states where assembly elections are scheduled next year.In a letter addressed to the chief secretaries and chief electoral officers of Goa, Manipur, Punjab, Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand, the commission said such individuals must maintain political neutrality and refrain from participating in election campaigns."The Commission has in the past, in respect of the conduct of government employees, issued instructions stating that they are not expected to take part in any election campaign or canvassing and should take scrupulous care not to lend their names, official position or authority to assist one individual/political party/group as against another," the letter read."Individuals including retired government officials/officers/employees are attached or engaged or employed or re-employed in various capacities by State/UT governments, for whom there are no specific guidelines or rules relating to their political neutrality and conduct during MCC period," it added.Assembly elections are due in all five states in 2027, with polls expected to be held in February-March. The terms of the Manipur, Goa, Punjab and Uttarakhand assemblies end in March, while the Uttar Pradesh assembly's term expires in May.Get the latest India News and Live updates.
