articles.title: A federal judge halted Trump's border wall work across Texas's 500-mile Big Bend sector; 38 days later, the Supreme Court cleared construction to resume while the lawsuit continues
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump has a penchant for dreaming up big projects, from his long-promised wall along the US-Mexico border to sweeping plans for
articles.body: US President Donald Trump has a penchant for dreaming up big projects, from his long-promised wall along the US-Mexico border to sweeping plans for reshaping federal buildings and public spaces. But one of his most ambitious border-security projects has run into a legal battle over its impact on one of America's most striking natural landscapes. On November 9, the US Supreme Court cleared the way for his administration to resume construction in Texas's Big Bend region, just 38 days after a federal judge ordered work to stop over concerns that the government had exceeded its authority to bypass environmental laws, as per a report by CBS News.The ruling allows construction of border barriers and related infrastructure across the Big Bend sector, which covers more than 500 miles of the US-Mexico border and includes Big Bend National Park. The Supreme Court's decision temporarily pauses a lower court's injunction while the legal challenge continues. It does not settle the underlying dispute over whether the administration can lawfully proceed with the project. The case has become a major test of how far the federal government can go in using its authority to accelerate border construction, particularly in environmentally sensitive areas.Why did a judge halt construction?The dispute began after the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) announced plans in February 2026 to expand border barriers and roads through the Big Bend region. Then-Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem issued waivers allowing construction to bypass several federal environmental and historic-preservation requirements. Her successor, Markwayne Mullin, issued additional waivers. The administration invoked a 1996 federal immigration law that gives the DHS secretary authority to waive legal requirements considered necessary to ensure the rapid construction of border barriers and roads near the southern border.The project includes 30-foot-tall steel bollard walls in certain areas, vehicle barriers, patrol roads and surveillance infrastructure. Government filings described plans for barriers and roads extending more than 300 miles in the region, although the wider Big Bend Border Patrol sector covers approximately 517 miles.Environmental groups, a local river guide and a religious organisation challenged the waivers in court in April. They argued that the administration had used a law intended to address areas of high illegal entry to justify construction in a region that records some of the lowest migrant apprehension numbers along the US-Mexico border.On October 2, US District Judge Kathleen Cardone granted a preliminary injunction, stopping construction and other ground-disturbing activities across the Big Bend sector. In her subsequent written opinion, she found that the challengers were likely to establish that the administration had exceeded its authority when issuing the waivers. The judge also questioned the government's description of Big Bend as an area of high illegal entry. The plaintiffs pointed out that the sector accounts for a relatively small share of apprehensions despite covering a substantial portion of the border.What did the Supreme Court decide?The Trump administration appealed to the Supreme Court, arguing that the lower court's order was obstructing its ability to secure the border and combat drug trafficking and illegal crossings. On November 9, the justices granted the administration's emergency request and temporarily lifted the injunction. The unsigned decision said the lower court's order was delaying construction and impeding the government's ability to advance its interests in border security. Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson was the lone dissenter, saying she would have rejected the administration's request for emergency relief.The ruling is an interim victory for Trump, but it does not mean the environmental groups have lost their lawsuit. The legal challenge will continue, and the Supreme Court's decision allows construction to proceed while the broader questions are considered.The administration has argued that more than 89,000 people attempting to cross into the US illegally were apprehended in the Big Bend sector between 2021 and 2025. It has also cited drug seizures and the activities of criminal cartels in neighbouring parts of Mexico, warning that leaving gaps in border protection could encourage trafficking and illegal entry. The challengers, however, maintain that the region's rugged terrain already makes illegal crossings difficult and that the scale of the proposed construction is unnecessary.Why is the Big Bend region controversial?The proposed project has drawn attention because of the landscape it could alter. Big Bend is known for its desert ecosystems, dramatic canyons, mountains and the Rio Grande, which forms part of the US-Mexico boundary. The wider area includes Big Bend National Park, Big Bend Ranch State Park and sections of the Rio Grande Wild and Scenic River corridor.Environmental groups and local residents argue that construction could fragment wildlife habitats, damage historic and cultural sites, disturb vegetation and affect access to the river. They have also raised concerns about the consequences for tourism, ranching and businesses that depend on the region's natural landscape. The opposition has extended beyond environmental organisations. Local landowners, cattle ranchers, river guides and politicians from both parties have questioned whether a large physical barrier is necessary in an area with relatively low migrant apprehension numbers.The administration, meanwhile, says it is not planning to construct a continuous 30-foot pedestrian wall through Big Bend National Park itself. Customs and Border Protection has said the park would instead see patrol roads, surveillance equipment and approximately 17 miles of vehicle barriers. The broader project also involves construction on private and public land outside the park.A much larger border-wall ambitionThe Big Bend project is part of Trump's wider effort to expand physical barriers along the southern border, a promise that has been central to his immigration agenda for more than a decade. Congress allocated approximately $46 billion for border-wall projects, allowing the administration to accelerate construction across several sections of the frontier. The Big Bend portion has been particularly contentious because of its ecological and cultural significance. According to reporting by The Washington Post, the project in the region has been estimated at around $1.7 billion.Construction activity had already begun in parts of the area before the legal intervention. Images of bulldozers clearing land near Big Bend National Park triggered criticism from environmentalists and lawmakers, prompting officials to announce a temporary pause on work inside the park.With the Supreme Court now allowing construction to resume, the administration can move ahead while the lawsuit remains unresolved. For conservationists and local communities, however, the concern is that damage to the desert, river corridor and wildlife habitats could be difficult to reverse even if the courts eventually rule against the project.You use AI every day. articles.title: Who is Ahmed Moor? Gaza-born Palestinian-American writer takes on John Fetterman in 2028 Pennsylvania Senate race
articles.summary: Ahmed Moor, a Palestinian-American writer, enters the Pennsylvania Senate race against John Fetterman, advocating for healthcare, housing, and ending military aid to Israel. Discover his campaign's broader goals and positions.
articles.body: Ahmed Moor, a Palestinian-American writer and journalist born in Gaza, has entered the race for the US Senate in Pennsylvania, announcing a Democratic primary challenge to incumbent John Fetterman for the 2028 election.Aged 42, Moor is campaigning for free healthcare, childcare, affordable housing and stronger civil liberties. He also supports ending US military aid to Israel, putting him at odds with Fetterman's pro-Israel stance.Moor has said his campaign is not simply an attempt to unseat the Pennsylvania senator. Speaking to The Philadelphia Inquirer, he described his motivation as a broader effort to change how the government works.“I'm not really running against Fetterman. I'm running for good government. I'm running for the rule of law. I'm running because I believe in America,” he told the newspaper.Who is Ahmed Moor?Moor was born in Rafah, a city in southern Gaza, and is a Palestinian-American writer and journalist. He has spoken publicly about his Palestinian background and his views on US policy towards Israel.His political positions include withdrawing American aid from Israel and imposing sanctions to secure equal rights for Palestinians. These proposals place him on a different footing from Fetterman, who has consistently defended Israel's military campaign in Gaza following the October 7, 2023, Hamas attack.What does Moor stand for?Moor has described his programme as a “dignity agenda”, with proposals including free healthcare, free childcare and affordable housing.In a post on X announcing his Senate bid, he also identified ending the war in Iran as a campaign priority. He called for accountability over what he described as genocide, the actions of Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), and corruption. Protecting civil liberties in the US was another commitment he outlined.His criticism extends beyond Republican policies. Moor has expressed little confidence in the Democratic Party's current leadership, arguing that it needs to respond more effectively to the country's political and constitutional challenges.He has also backed stronger restrictions on corporate and special-interest influence in government, making political accountability a central part of his campaign message.Why is he challenging John Fetterman?Moor's candidacy comes as Fetterman faces criticism from Democrats over his voting record and support for Republicans on several issues, particularly Israel.Fetterman entered the Senate in 2023 after campaigning as a progressive outsider. However, his positions have since disappointed some Democrats who supported his 2022 campaign. He has also received praise from President Donald Trump, who has described him as “a great guy” and said he would welcome him into the Republican Party.The senator has said he has no intention of leaving the Democrats, but warned last year that he would reconsider if the party formally adopted an anti-Israel position.Moor's campaign presents a direct policy contrast, particularly over US support for Israel. However, he has framed his candidacy around a wider set of domestic and foreign policy priorities rather than solely as a challenge to the incumbent.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Woman killed with brick after argument with Facebook friend in Ghaziabad’s Loni
articles.summary: GHAZIABAD: A woman was allegedly killed by a man she had befriended on Facebook around four to five months ago following an argument during their meeting
articles.body: GHAZIABAD: A woman was allegedly killed by a man she had befriended on Facebook around four to five months ago following an argument during their meeting in Ghaziabad’s Loni Border area on Monday.The deceased has been identified as Pinky, a native of Bulandshahr, while the accused, identified as Pintu, also hails from the same district.According to police, the incident came to light on Monday when the Indrapuri police outpost, under the Loni Border police station, received information about the murder of a woman. A police team, accompanied by senior officers, immediately reached the spot and inspected the crime scene.During preliminary inquiries, police discovered that Pinky and Pintu had come into contact through Facebook approximately four to five months ago. They subsequently began communicating over phone calls and developed a friendship.On Monday, Pintu reportedly visited Pinky to meet her. However, an argument broke out between them over an issue that is yet to be established.Police said the altercation escalated when Pintu allegedly picked up a brick lying nearby and struck Pinky on the head, causing fatal injuries.ACP Ankur Vihar Amardeep Maurya said the woman's body was taken into custody and sent for post-mortem examination after completing the necessary legal formalities."The two had become friends through Facebook around four to five months ago. The accused visited the woman on Monday, and an argument broke out between them. He allegedly attacked her on the head with a brick, resulting in her death," Maurya said.Police are questioning the accused to ascertain the circumstances surrounding the incident and the motive behind the alleged attack.Further legal proceedings are underway, while investigators are examining the sequence of events that led to the woman's death.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Ghaziabad | Silver Rate in Ghaziabad | Bank Holidays in Ghaziabad | Public Holidays in Ghaziabad | Ghaziabad AQI | Weather in Ghaziabad | Petrol Price in Ghaziabad | Diesel Price in Ghaziabad | CNG Price in Ghaziabad | LPG Price in GhaziabadStay updated with the latest Ghaziabad news. articles.title: UK seeks military hotline with Russia amid fears accidental clash could spark war
articles.summary: Britain and Russia should establish fresh lines of communication, particularly between their military establishments, to reduce the risk of a
articles.body: Britain and Russia should establish fresh lines of communication, particularly between their military establishments, to reduce the risk of a miscalculation amid rising tensions, UK defence secretary Wes Streeting has said. He warned that Moscow's alleged state-sponsored terrorism and growing hostile activities against Britain make direct communication increasingly important.In an interview with the Financial Times (FT), Streeting said Britain should have additional channels of contact with Moscow beyond its embassy, including direct military-to-military communication.“We have our embassy in Moscow. That is an important channel . . . I would much prefer there to be additional channels too, particularly military-to-military level,” he told the newspaper.“There is always a risk of miscalculation and that’s why having that direct communication is important.”The remarks come as Britain seeks to restore diplomatic and defence communication with Russia but has so far faced resistance from Moscow. UK officials said London had attempted to reopen backchannels with senior Russian defence officials, but its efforts had been rebuffed.“Right now, it feels that miscalculation is a greater risk than a deliberate move to escalate,” one government figure told the FT.No conversations between a serving British chief of defence staff or defence secretary and their Russian counterparts have taken place since 2022, following Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.UK lags behind France, Germany in Russia contactsBritain has fallen behind European allies such as France and Germany in maintaining political and diplomatic contact with Russian President Vladimir Putin's government.In September, German foreign minister Johann Wadephul met his Russian counterpart Sergey Lavrov on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly. It was the first meeting between the two countries' foreign ministers since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.The meeting followed Berlin's accusations that Russian intelligence had attempted a drone attack at Leipzig airport.France has also taken steps to reopen communication with Moscow. President Emmanuel Macron sent his diplomatic adviser Emmanuel Bonne to meet senior Russian officials in February. Macron had also spoken to Putin in July 2025, ending a three-year gap in direct communication.The Trump administration has maintained even closer high-level contact with Moscow. Trilateral peace talks involving the United States, Russia and Ukraine are scheduled to take place in Abu Dhabi from Tuesday.UK accuses Russia of state-sponsored terrorismStreeting also highlighted the growing threat posed by Russia, saying Britain had witnessed several hostile activities that went beyond conventional military threats.“We have seen over the course of this year numerous examples of what some people call hybrid threats, and I prefer to call state-sponsored terrorism,” he said.Russia has increasingly portrayed Britain as a leading adversary in the West, partly because of London's prominent role in Nato's support for Ukraine.In March, Alexander Bortnikov, head of Russia's domestic intelligence agency FSB, described Britain as the “puppet master of Ukraine's secret services”.Other incidents have added to tensions. A Russian warship fired warning shots at a British yacht in the Channel this summer. A Russian military aircraft was also accused of flying dangerously close to the Royal Navy aircraft carrier HMS Prince of Wales.Moscow has also been linked to alleged arson attacks, interference with undersea cables and cyber attacks.A former British national security official said Moscow's reluctance to engage with London was also part of its broader strategy.“Part of Russia’s shtick is to say the UK is unimportant and does not warrant engagement, so setting up and managing these channels is part of the mind judo of Anglo-Russian relations,” the former official said.Streeting warns EU against excluding UK from defence purchasesSeparately, Streeting warned that the European Union's proposed 'Made in Europe' rules could weaken Nato by limiting economic cooperation between allies.The rules are intended to strengthen European manufacturers. However, Streeting urged the bloc not to use them to restrict British companies from participating in its defence procurement programmes.He raised the issue during meetings last week with EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas and Defence Commissioner Andrius Kubilius.“We’ve got to hold true to the strength of our alliance through the economic lens as well as the military lens,” he said, pointing to the impact of the United States' “America First” protectionist policies.Streeting was speaking ahead of the Atlantic Future Forum conference in Oslo, which is being held aboard HMS Prince of Wales. The conference will examine lessons from the Ukraine war for European security.He also stressed the importance of sovereign capabilities and control over critical technology, particularly artificial intelligence, following concerns over Ukraine's access to the US-based Starlink satellite network.UK keeps door open to more military support for Saudi ArabiaStreeting also indicated that Britain could provide further military assistance to Saudi Arabia as it faces attacks from Yemen's Houthi rebels.Last month, Britain deployed RAF Typhoon fighter jets, a heavy-lift transport aircraft and military advisers to support Riyadh following requests for assistance.“It’s really important that the UK is seen by our friends and allies as a partner that shows up when help is needed . . . We’ll continue to work closely with our friends in Saudi to understand their needs and requirements,” he said.However, he ruled out Britain being drawn into the wider conflict, stressing that a diplomatic solution was necessary.“What we don’t want to do is get dragged into the war,” he said, adding that a “diplomatic resolution” rather than a “military route” was the only way to end the conflict.You use AI every day. articles.title: In 2019, oil was found seeping from a California railyard into the Sacramento River; six years later, cleanup had removed 75,000 gallons of oil and 100,000 tons of contaminated soil.
articles.summary: We measure pollution by what we can see: smoke rising from factories, plastic floating in rivers, or oil spreading across the surface of water.
articles.body: We measure pollution by what we can see: smoke rising from factories, plastic floating in rivers, or oil spreading across the surface of water. But some of the most persistent environmental damage happens quietly, beneath the ground, sometimes for generations. Among those hidden places, A railway yard may seem like an unlikely place for an environmental crisis, but what lies beneath the ground can sometimes be more dangerous than what meets the eye. And that's exactly what happened in California, US.In Dunsmuir, California, oil from an old locomotive-fuelling facility had been leaking into the surrounding soil and the Sacramento River for decades. It was not until in 2019, that the scale of the contamination came forward only when authorities began investigating the seepage.The investigation revealed that the problem was much older than initially understood. According to the US Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), the contamination could be traced back to the early 1900s, when leaking tanks and equipment were used to fuel locomotives at the railyard. Over the years, oil accumulated in the surrounding soil and continued to seep towards the river.In 2021, the EPA began working with the California Department of Fish and Wildlife, the Central Valley Regional Water Quality Control Board and Union Pacific Railroad to address the source of the contamination. The cleanup involved removing oil-contaminated soil, dealing with the seepage along the riverbank and restoring the affected shoreline.How did authorities clean up the decades-old oil contamination?The cleanup was a multi-year operation that involved removing contaminated soil and oil from the railyard and rebuilding the affected riverbank. Crews first excavated the oil-contaminated soil and removed portions of an existing retaining wall along the Sacramento River. They then brought in clean soil and installed a special barrier fill designed to prevent any remaining oil from seeping into the river.The work also involved restoring around 1,400 feet of the affected shoreline, improving the river's capacity and creating additional habitat for wildlife. By November 2025, the US Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) had completed its oversight of the major removal work, which had taken out approximately 75,000 gallons of oil and 100,000 tons of contaminated soil. What does the cleanup mean for the Sacramento River and its wildlife?The restoration work was particularly important because the Upper Sacramento River is not just a waterway passing through the region; it is also an important watershed and wildlife habitat. During the earlier stages of the response, crews used oil-absorbing materials near known seepage points to capture oil before it could spread. They also placed oil-retention booms in the fast-flowing river and removed contaminated gravel and stones from sections of the riverbed, replacing them with absorbent materials. These measures were intended to limit the movement of oil downstream and reduce further exposure to the surrounding environment.However, cleaning up an ecosystem is not as simple as removing the visible signs of pollution. The river and its banks need to be monitored to understand whether contamination is still present and whether the restored habitat is holding up. During the 2024 work, authorities regularly checked the water for oil and turbidity, collecting measurements upstream, downstream and near the construction site. This was especially important because removing the old retaining wall and excavating contaminated soil could disturb sediment and release trapped oil into the water.Even after the major cleanup was completed in 2025, monitoring remained necessary. In October 2026, oil was once again observed seeping from the soil along a section of the restored shoreline. Response teams installed containment barriers and booms, while crews removed additional contaminated sand and gravel. The authorities reported that no oiled wildlife had been observed during this response.Pollution does not always announce itself. Sometimes, it remains buried beneath layers of soil, quietly affecting the environment for decades before anyone realises the scale of the damage. The story of the Dunsmuir railyard is a reminder that environmental damage can outlast the industries and activities that caused it. Removing 75,000 gallons of oil and 100,000 tons of contaminated soil was a significant step, but the fresh seepage reported in 2026 shows that the work is far from over. Nature may have the ability to recover, but that recovery requires more than a one-time cleanup. It demands sustained attention, accountability and the willingness to repair damage long after it has been caused.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Richard Simmons' Los Angeles home sells for $3.8 million after decades of ownership; inside the fitness icon's unusual residence with a key-shaped swimming pool
articles.summary: Richard Simmons’ Los Angeles home has sold for $3.8 million, ending a long chapter for the hilltop estate where the fitness icon lived for more than four
articles.body: Richard Simmons’ Los Angeles home has sold for $3.8 million, ending a long chapter for the hilltop estate where the fitness icon lived for more than four decades. Set high above the Sunset Strip, the gated property offers panoramic city views, terraced gardens, an attic gym and a key-shaped pool. Simmons bought the four-bedroom residence in the 1980s and filled it with eccentric decoration that mirrored his vibrant public persona. He died there in July 2024, and the house has since passed through a sales campaign, several price cuts and a change in marketing approach before finding its new owner.Richard Simmons’ estate finally finds a buyer after months of price cuts and a bold relaunchAccording to Market Watch, the house first reached the market at $6.99 million in June 2025, 11 months after Simmons died. Its price was cut several times, with the latest reduction in May leaving it at $5.8 million. In April, the home made a return to the market with what listing agents Rachelle Rosten and Kelly deLaat of Douglas Elliman called a “highly strategic” sales approach, designed to maximise how buyers viewed its potential. The final price is roughly $3.2 million below where the listing began, and the sale completed more than two years after Simmons’ death.Agents repositioned the home as a development opportunity, valuing the land over the house itselfThe new strategy followed what Rosten told Realtor was a careful reassessment of the property’s full potential. She said it was never meant to erase Simmons’ legacy, but to give it new life, and that the true value lies in the land rather than the existing house.The reasoning was practical. The current home occupies only a small portion of the 0.56-acre parcel, which rises in several usable tiers, with flat pads, terraced gardens and a dedicated pool level. That left room for a much larger modern mansion, whether built out from the existing structure or from scratch.Staircase cherubs, patterned wallpaper and curved French doors gave the home its joyful personalityRosten acknowledged that the property’s celebrity provenance and distinctive design details would generate significant interest, though she suggested these were unlikely to be what clinched a sale. She pointed to the staircase cherubs, vibrant patterned wallpaper and curved French patio doors as touches that make the house both memorable and visually striking.Many people close to Simmons described the home as a deeply personal sanctuary. Spanning nearly 5,000 square feet, with four and a half bathrooms, it reflects a man who built an empire encouraging millions to exercise through his hugely successful “Sweatin’ to the Oldies” workout videos.Disguises and quiet drives; how Richard Simmons lived behind closed doors in his final yearsThe house drew fresh attention in May, when broadcast journalist Diane Sawyer visited to spend time with Simmons’ brother, Lenny Simmons, and his housekeeper, Teresa Reveles, for a special that aired on 12 May.Reveles told Sawyer that Simmons gradually withdrew from public life and ventured out only when he was sure nobody would recognise him. She said he often disguised himself in elaborate costumes, from clown outfits to women’s clothing, and that she would then drive him around the city so he could see its new buildings and shops.Reveles also described the days before his death. He had fallen the night before he died but was reluctant to seek medical attention, telling those around him that he simply wanted to stay at home. His final evening, she recalled, was spent watching television, eating dinner and speaking of his gratitude for his life and his supporters before going to bed.“The perfect buyer found this home,” Rosten told Realtor. Drawn to its rich history, heritage and pedigree, she said, the buyer plans to restore it to its classic roots. That is a notably different path from the redevelopment the listing had invited. Paul Czako of Gussman Czako Estates represented the buyer.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.body: NEW DELHI: Union minister Kiren Rijiju on Tuesday slammed Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi for attacking Prime Minister Narendra Modi over his remarks on 'Dimagi Naxal'.In a social media post on X, Rijiju reminded Rahul that former Prime Minister Manmohan Singh had described Left-wing extremism as the biggest internal security threat to the country."Rahul ji, thank Modi ji for eliminating the Armed Maoists. Former PM Dr Manmohan Singh ji had famously described Left-Wing Extremism and Naxalism as 'The single biggest internal security threat' to India," Rijiju said."Next target is to finish Dimagi Naxals," he added.This comes a day after Rahul hit back at PM Modi over his 'Dimagi Naxal' remarks, claiming that the CRPF jawans' facial expressions suggested they did not believe the Prime Minister's claims.In a post on X addressed to CRPF personnel who attended PM Modi's Diwali event in Bastar, Rahul said, "Your faces said it all: you didn't buy the PM's lies. He called us Naxals.""My challenge stands. Let him debate me on who is anti-national and who is controlled by foreign forces. Any time, any place," he said, adding, "My guarantee: after the debate, the PM won't have the guts to stand in front of a single jawan again."The war of words began after PM Modi, while celebrating Diwali with security personnel in Bastar, Chhattisgarh, said that although armed Naxalites had been wiped out from forests, "Dimagi Naxals" had infiltrated several organisations and political parties and were inciting people against the Constitution and democracy.The Prime Minister also accused previous governments of restricting the freedom of security personnel engaged in anti-Naxal operations, saying his government had given them the authority to take necessary decisions."We must remember one thing. articles.title: In 1944, a German U-boat sank the SS Cornwallis off Maine, killing 43 sailors; 82 years later, a dive team ended a seven-year search by locating the wreck almost 400 feet underwater in July 2026
articles.summary: In a world where miles feel like inches, almost everybody is connected to each other.
articles.body: In a world where miles feel like inches, almost everybody is connected to each other. The whole world has become one village; yet the ocean floor still remains one of the most mysterious places for scientists. You’d be surprised to know that scientists now know more about outer space than they do about the ocean floor.The ocean has a way of holding on to secrets, sometimes for decades and even centuries. Beneath its vast surface lie the remains of ships that once carried people, cargo and stories, many of which were never meant to be forgotten. One such story dates back to the Second World War, when a German submarine torpedoed a Canadian merchant ship off the coast of Maine, sending it beneath the waves in a matter of minutes.On December 3, 1944, the SS Cornwallis was travelling along the Maine coast when it was struck by a torpedo fired by German submarine U-1230. Of the 48 people aboard, only five survived. For more than 80 years, the ship's final resting place remained a mystery. However, in July 2026, a team of divers finally located the wreck, nearly 400 feet beneath the surface, bringing a decades-old search to an end.What happened to the SS Cornwallis in 1944?Imagine being aboard a ship, sailing across the Atlantic, with the journey almost nearing its end. The crew had no reason to believe that this ordinary voyage would turn into a tragedy. The SS Cornwallis had left Barbados on November 20, 1944, carrying bags of sugar and barrels of molasses, and was heading towards Saint John, New Brunswick. However, as the ship travelled along the New England coast on December 3, it encountered a German submarine, U-1230.Commanded by Hans Hilbig, the submarine fired a torpedo that struck the forward section of the Cornwallis. The impact was devastating, and the ship began sinking by the bow, disappearing beneath the water in less than 10 minutes.As per the Canadian Virtual War Memorial, out of the 48 people aboard, six managed to escape in a lifeboat. Although they were eventually rescued by a fishing boat, one of them died from hypothermia. In the devastating attack, only five survived, while 43 people lost their lives.How did the dive team finally locate the wreck after seven years?Finding a shipwreck that has remained lost for more than eight decades is no easy task, especially when it lies hundreds of feet beneath the ocean. For the Nomad Exploration Team, the search for the SS Cornwallis began in 2019 and involved years of research, multiple expeditions and hours spent studying historical records.The team first narrowed down three possible locations using historical records, including the coordinates from the ship's distress call, reports of debris spotted from the air and the location where fishermen had rescued the survivors. They also studied historical weather conditions, tide charts and the ship's blueprints to understand where it might have gone down. Over five expeditions, the divers scanned more than 50 square miles of the ocean floor.However, the discovery almost slipped through their hands. On July 11, 2026, during their fifth search expedition, the team was scanning the final stretch of a search grid when the shipwreck appeared on their sonar. They had actually passed close to the wreck once before without recognising it. This time, a more sophisticated side-scan sonar device helped them capture a clearer image of the vessel.But a sonar image alone was not enough to establish its identity. The divers eventually descended nearly 400 feet beneath the surface to examine the wreck themselves. By comparing the remains with the original blueprints of the SS Cornwallis, they confirmed that they had finally found the missing ship.What makes the discovery of the SS Cornwallis historically significant?The discovery is particularly significant because the sinking of the SS Cornwallis was connected to a wider German operation along the American coast. Just four days before the attack, German submarine U-1230 had landed two German spies, Erich Gimpel and William Colepaugh, in Maine. The discovery of the wreck therefore brings renewed attention to an important chapter of the Second World War and helps researchers understand the maritime history of the region.The ocean floor is perhaps one of the few places where history can remain untouched for generations, waiting to be discovered. The finding of the SS Cornwallis is not simply about locating a sunken ship; it is also about bringing back a story that had remained beneath the waves for more than eight decades. While the wreck may have finally been found, the 43 people who lost their lives remain an important part of its history. Sometimes, discovering the past is also a way of ensuring that it is not forgotten.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Children's Hospital Los Angeles raises record $1.35 billion in fundraising campaign supported by Jimmy Kimmel and Jamie Lee Curtis
articles.summary: Children’s Hospital Los Angeles (CHLA) has raised a record $1.35 billion through its 125th Anniversary Campaign, with the support of thousands of donors,
articles.body: Children’s Hospital Los Angeles (CHLA) has raised a record $1.35 billion through its 125th Anniversary Campaign, with the support of thousands of donors, including honorary campaign chairs Jimmy Kimmel, Jamie Lee Curtis, Sugar Ray Leonard and Chuck Lorre. This is the largest fundraising effort in CHLA’s history. The funds will help advance paediatric care, medical research and education for children and families.From one horseback visit to a global nameIn 1901, Children’s Hospital Los Angeles opened in a small house dedicated to children, and its first year brought 14 patients. One physician led the work and travelled on horseback to reach young patients across the region. Today, the hospital oversees more than 750,000 patient visits a year, drawing families from across the United States and more than 90 countries. The change came in steps. In 1930, its physicians performed the first paediatric heart surgery on the West Coast. In 1978, it built a comprehensive paediatric cancer programme, and it now runs one of the first and largest CAR T-cell therapy programmes in the country. By 1993, it had joined early gene therapy research for a rare inherited immune disorder. Its training programmes for paediatricians, nurses and researchers are among the largest in the country. Paul S. Viviano, the hospital’s president and CEO, puts it simply: the team has “continually pushed the boundaries of care”.A night that started with a patient’s familyThe fundraising campaign was held at The Event Deck at L.A. LIVE, bringing together philanthropists, community leaders, celebrities, patients and supporters to celebrate the historic achievement. Gina Rodriguez, the Golden Globe-winning actress who hosted the evening, opened the event by talking about her own experience. Her daughter, Lucy, was treated at the hospital’s Neurological Institute. “Today Lucy is totally fine and everyone we encountered during our time at CHLA was absolutely amazing,” Rodriguez said. “I’m thrilled to show my appreciation by welcoming you here tonight to honour the amazing supporters of the hospital and enjoy some outstanding entertainment.”The evening also featured Grammy winner Michael Bublé, who sang hits including “Fly Me to the Moon” and “Feeling Good”.Nikki DeLoach and Jeffrey Worthe co-chaired the campaign. Both have long served the hospital. The honorary campaign chairs include Jimmy Kimmel, Sugar Ray Leonard, Chuck Lorre and Jamie Lee Curtis.Paul S. Viviano, the hospital’s president and chief executive, credited thousands of donors, corporate partners, foundations, families and staff members. He said the money would help the hospital stay at the forefront of paediatric medicine and accelerate scientific discoveries. “Thanks to the remarkable generosity of our supporters, CHLA will continue to be at the forefront of paediatric medicine, accelerate scientific discoveries and ensure children have access to world-class care for generations to come.”Two longtime supporters honouredThe event also recognised the campaign’s longtime supporters: radio personality and host Ellen K, and Kourtney and Justin Turner. They were honoured with The Courage to Care Award. Ellen K’s ties to the hospital began when her son, Calvin, received emergency care after a serious injury. Since then, she has helped raise more than $4 million through KOST 103.5’s annual Giving Tuesday broadcast. “As a forever-grateful mom and as a member of the Board of Trustees, I will continue showing up for CHLA in every way I can,” she said.Kourtney and Justin Turner were recognised for more than a decade of volunteering, fundraising and advocacy. Through the Justin Turner Foundation, they have supported children facing serious illnesses. Justin Turner recalled that when he played for the Dodgers, the hospital was almost on his way home from the stadium. “It has been a gift to get involved with this hospital. When I was with the Dodgers, CHLA was literally on my way home from the stadium. I visited as much as I could, and so did Kourtney. Children’s Hospital Los Angeles is one of the most amazing institutions in our city.”Drew Barrymore, Jamie Lee Curtis, Pau Gasol, Heidi Klum, Natalie Portman, the LA Kings, Panda Express, The Walt Disney Company, Chuck Lorre, Bernadette and Sugar Ray Leonard, and AEG were among the past recipients of the Courage to Care Award.Meanwhile, Olympian Jordan Chiles presented a Mission Moment highlighting the Jackie and Gene Autry Orthopedic Center, which treats thousands of children with bone and joint conditions every year. The centre runs one of the largest paediatric spine and neuromuscular programmes in the country and offers services in hip preservation, sports medicine, and hand and upper extremity care.The night ended with Bublé performing some of his most beloved hits, including ‘You’re Nobody Till Somebody Loves You’, ‘Fly Me to the Moon’, ‘Such A Night’, ‘Haven’t Met You Yet’, ‘Feeling Good’ and ‘Song For You’.“It’s really special to be here tonight and perform for Children’s Hospital Los Angeles, which means so much to my family. Our family knows firsthand how much the people here care. We’ll always be grateful for the way they were there for us and for everything they do for kids and families,” Bublé said.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Lindsay Clancy case: Judge rejects bid to dismiss murder charges, paving way for possible retrial
articles.summary: A Massachusetts judge ruled against Lindsay Clancy's attempt to dismiss murder charges, citing sufficient grounds for a mistrial. The next trial date is suggested for March 2027, as the prosecution contemplates further actions.
articles.body: A Massachusetts judge has rejected Lindsay Clancy's request to dismiss the murder charges against her, ruling that a second trial over the deaths of her three children would not violate her constitutional protection against double jeopardy.Judge William Sullivan ruled on Monday that there was sufficient legal justification for declaring her first trial a mistrial in September. He also rejected a prosecution request for a gag order restricting public statements by the parties involved in the case.The ruling follows arguments presented last week by Clancy's defence team, which maintained that holding another trial would amount to double jeopardy. Her lawyers argued that the judge had not exhausted all available options to resolve a disagreement among jurors before ending the first trial.Sullivan disagreed, concluding that there was a legal basis for the mistrial under the principle of “manifest necessity”. The standard requires that all reasonable options for reaching a verdict be exhausted before a trial can be terminated.In his ruling, the judge also rejected claims that the juror responsible for the deadlock had refused to participate in deliberations.“The foreperson's notes did not plausibly suggest that Juror Doe refused to consider the trial evidence or disagreed with the law as explained by the Court in its instructions,” Sullivan wrote as cited by CNN.He added that information about the juror that emerged after the trial could not be used to challenge the decision to declare a mistrial.The defence had sought access to records relating to the juror, including his phone records and jury selection questionnaire. Sullivan denied the request, saying the material was not relevant to the motion to dismiss or any potential retrial. He also found no grounds to require the juror to testify under oath.The juror, identified as Michael Péguy Desronvil, had faced public scrutiny after the first trial ended. He subsequently said that accounts given by some fellow jurors to the media had misrepresented his position.Sullivan also indicated that he was considering March 2027 for the next trial, with the parties expected to return to court next Monday to discuss scheduling.However, the Plymouth County District Attorney's Office has not formally confirmed whether it intends to prosecute Clancy again. Prosecutors remained noncommittal during last week's hearing and declined to comment on Monday's developments.Clancy's defence attorney, Kevin Reddington, had questioned the prosecution's delay in deciding whether to pursue another trial and what charges his client might face.In a separate ruling, Sullivan rejected prosecutors' request for restrictions on statements made by Clancy's legal team outside court. He said the prosecution had not demonstrated that those comments posed a serious risk of prejudicing jury selection or the outcome of a future trial.The judge said prosecutors could renew their request if circumstances changed, while reminding the defence team of its professional obligations.You use AI every day. articles.title: 'No, I won't let our baby be thrown into river': Sonia recalls loss of first child before Rahul
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: In September 1968, the Gandhi household was filled with joy when Sonia Gandhi announced her pregnancy.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: In September 1968, the Gandhi household was filled with joy when Sonia Gandhi announced her pregnancy. Even the usually stern Indira Gandhi broke into a rare display of affection, embracing her daughter-in-law Sonia Gandhi and exclaiming, “One big baby having another baby!”But the happiness was short-lived.Sonia gave birth to a premature baby boy on January 18, 1969, two months before her due date. Initially overjoyed, the family was soon devastated by the newborn’s death.In her newly released memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love, Sonia recounts the deeply personal tragedy for the first time. She writes that the baby was buried by her husband Rajiv Gandhi and brother-in-law Sanjay Gandhi at Feroze Gandhi’s farmhouse in Mehrauli.“I heard the baby's first cry as he was placed in the incubator. Later Rajiv took me to see him, a tiny, perfectly formed boy, with thick, black hair and long, slim fingers. We gazed at him together, Rajiv's arm around my shoulder. We fell in love with him immediately,” she writes.Doctors had warned Rajiv that the baby’s chances of survival were uncertain. At 6:30 am, he was informed that the newborn had died.“With Amie Aunty beside him, he broke it gently to me when at 6:30 in the morning the end came. ‘No it was not possible! Why, why,’ I kept asking. Both of us were shocked and heartbroken, we held each other tight. I cried my heart out, and Rajiv, in spite of his ‘stiff upper lip’ upbringing, also wept copiously,” she recalls.Indira, who was away on a tour, cut short her visit and rushed to the hospital.“She embraced us, her eyes red and swollen, and sat with us for a long time. She wanted to remain with us, she said, but had to complete her tour engagement. She left early the next morning, full of sorrow: She, too, had so looked forward to the happy event.”The family then faced the difficult question of the newborn’s last rites. Sonia writes that, according to Hindu tradition, a newborn could not be cremated and was traditionally released into a river.However, the thought brought back a disturbing memory of seeing a swollen male body trapped near the Okhla barrage, with scavenging dogs trying to pull it out.“‘No,’ I whispered. ‘No matter what, I'm not going to allow our baby to be thrown into the river.’...’No, I couldn't do that to my baby, no matter how sacred the river was,’ I said, breaking into sobs. How could I consent to do something that seemed to me so alien and heartless to my tiny child, already deprived of his chance to live?”The family eventually decided to bury the child at Feroze Gandhi’s farmhouse in Mehrauli.“It was a painful and agonising option, but there was no other way. Rajiv came back to the hospital and told me that he and Sanjay had buried the little one deep under a beautiful pink bougainvillea bush, then in full bloom on the left side along the inner boundary wall," she recounts.“For a long time we'd pause and place a flower over the spot each time we went there. It didn't assuage our pain, but we had to accept the inevitable,” she writes.Sonia also recalls how Indira had closely monitored her pregnancy, advising her on diet, walks and exercise. She writes that she had no major discomfort, apart from missing Italian food and developing a craving for jamun, phalsa and Fanta, sometimes drinking twelve glasses a day.The loss left her depressed and struggling with feelings of inadequacy and guilt. The pain was compounded by a right-wing opposition newspaper publishing an article titled, "Indira Gandhi failed in her attempt to become the grandmother of a bastard child."“The venom of those words scarred my heart. How could people be so cruel? What had I done to deserve such malice? The hurt caused by that spiteful comment added to the heartbreak of my loss and to my feeling of inadequacy,” she writes.In October 1969, Sonia told Rajiv she was pregnant again. “Thrilled but anxious”, she gave birth to their second child, Rahul Gandhi, on June 19, 1970.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: 40% of trains cancelled, over 4,000 passengers affected as Spanish drivers strike after two fatal crashes
articles.summary: Spanish train drivers went on strike on Tuesday, demanding increased investment in maintenance and safety, days after at least 69 people were killed in a
articles.body: Spanish train drivers went on strike on Tuesday, demanding increased investment in maintenance and safety, days after at least 69 people were killed in a collision between a passenger train and a stationary train on the high-speed Madrid-Seville line on October 28.The crash was Spain’s second fatal train accident this year. An earlier accident in southern Spain, also on the Madrid-Seville line, in January claimed 46 lives.The strike led to widespread travel disruption across Spain. According to state-run train operator Renfe, 40% of long- and medium-distance services were cancelled on Tuesday, affecting 4,042 passengers. Around 90% of services on Madrid’s commuter network and 50% of local services in Barcelona, the country’s second-largest city, were also cancelled.In Leganes, near the capital, Madrid, commuters had to rely on buses to reach the city centre. At least five lines on the city’s commuter rail network were not operational, while three others were running partially, state operator Cercanias said.In the Catalonia region, operator Rodalies reported delays due to non-compliance with minimum service requirements. At Masnou station, on the outskirts of Barcelona, the regional capital, only a handful of passengers were seen waiting for the intermittent train service.Talks between the train drivers' union and the government on improving safety across Spain's high-speed rail network, the most extensive in Europe, began after the January crash but broke down in April, according to the union.The second collision occurred after a controller instructed a Renfe-operated train to proceed despite a signal failure, even though an Iryo-operated train was stationary further ahead on the same track.King Felipe VI and Queen Letizia were scheduled to join relatives of the victims of last month's crash at a funeral at Toledo Cathedral in central Spain later on Tuesday.Last week, Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez appointed his deputy, Carlos Cuerpo, to temporarily oversee the transport ministry after Oscar Puente stepped down following the two crashes on the Madrid-Seville line.(With Reuters inputs)You use AI every day. articles.title: Digital arrest scams: SC seeks prevention plan from WhatsApp & others, sends notice to RBI
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court has asked WhatsApp and other digital intermediaries to submit details of the measures they propose to take to prevent digital
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court has asked WhatsApp and other digital intermediaries to submit details of the measures they propose to take to prevent digital arrest scams and related cybercrimes, directing them to share their proposals with the Indian Cybercrime Coordination Centre (I4C) as well.A bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, also comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, issued the direction in an order uploaded on the court's website following a hearing on October 29.The matter has been listed for further hearing on November 23.The case, taken up suo motu, is titled ‘In Re: Victims of Digital Arrest Related to Forged Documents’.“WhatsApp LLC (A Meta company) and other concerned intermediaries are also directed to apprise this Court of the measures they propose to undertake to prevent the digital arrest scams and related cybercrimes. They shall also simultaneously submit their proposals to the I4C,” the bench said.SC wants banks to compensate digital fraud victimsThe court also reiterated its concerns over the role of financial institutions in preventing digital fraud, saying banks must be held accountable where their failure to exercise due diligence contributes to such crimes.In its October 29 order, the bench said the Reserve Bank of India's proposed regulatory measures must include provisions requiring financial institutions to compensate victims when an investigation establishes that fraud occurred due to their failure to prevent or report suspicious activity.“We reiterate and emphasize that the regulatory measures proposed by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) must mandate and incorporate suitable provisions that require financial institutions to indemnify victims of digital arrest scams and other cyber frauds and pay suitable compensation not less than the amount lost by the customer,” the bench said.SC seeks details of authorised financial institutions from RBITo ensure effective implementation of the proposed safeguards, the bench directed the RBI to submit a list of all authorised financial institutions before the next hearing.The court observed that although cybercrimes had declined by 50%, victims had still lost around Rs 800 crore so far this year.It said the RBI's proposed regulatory framework must include enforceable provisions for compensation, preventive intervention and institutional accountability.Describing banks as a “protective umbrella” for vulnerable customers, CJI Surya Kant said financial institutions had access to account holders' transaction histories and should use that information to identify and prevent fraudulent transfers before money leaves their accounts.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: In 2006, an African president's son bought a 16-acre Malibu estate for $30 million; after a US corruption settlement, it sold for $93.5 million in 2026, with a new report linking its buyer to the Chrome Hearts family
articles.summary: A 16-acre Malibu estate that once belonged to Teodoro Nguema Obiang, the son of Equatorial Guinea’s president, has entered another extraordinary chapter.
articles.body: A 16-acre Malibu estate that once belonged to Teodoro Nguema Obiang, the son of Equatorial Guinea’s president, has entered another extraordinary chapter. The property was bought for $30 million in 2006, later surrendered in a U.S. corruption settlement, and sold for $93.5 million in June 2026, according to Celebrity Net Worth and the U.S. Department of Justice. A new report cited by Celebrity Net Worth links the latest buyer to the family behind luxury fashion brand Chrome Hearts.The estate, located at 3620 Sweetwater Mesa Road in Malibu’s gated Serra Retreat community, overlooks the Pacific Ocean, Malibu Lagoon and Surfrider Beach. Its value has risen dramatically since the 2006 purchase, but its ownership history remains one of the most unusual in California real estateA lavish purchase in 2006Teodoro Nguema Obiang, commonly known as Teodorín, bought the Malibu mansion in April 2006 through a company called Sweetwater Malibu LLC. At the time, he was serving as Equatorial Guinea’s agriculture and forestry minister and reportedly earned less than $100,000 a year in his official government role.The purchase raised immediate questions because the $30 million price was vastly beyond his official income. The U.S. Department of Justice later alleged that Obiang had used his government position to amass more than $300 million in assets through corruption and money laundering.The mansion was only part of a much larger collection. Obiang was also known for owning a $38 million private jet, rare Ferraris and Lamborghinis, expensive artwork, a Paris mansion and millions of dollars in Michael Jackson memorabilia.The Malibu property itself was guarded by personnel from Equatorial Guinea, some of whom reportedly carried automatic weapons. The security arrangements added to the sense that the estate was not simply a luxury home, but part of a much larger international controversy.The U.S. corruption settlementIn October 2014, the U.S. Department of Justice announced a civil forfeiture settlement requiring Obiang to relinquish more than $30 million in assets purchased with corruption proceeds. The assets included the Malibu mansion, a Ferrari and various pieces of Michael Jackson memorabilia.Under the agreement, Obiang was required to sell the Malibu estate, with $20 million of the proceeds going to a charitable organization for the benefit of the people of Equatorial Guinea. Another $10.3 million was forfeited to the United States, with funds to be used for the benefit of the Equatoguinean people to the extent permitted by law.The settlement was part of the Justice Department’s Kleptocracy Asset Recovery Initiative, which aimed to recover assets allegedly obtained through foreign corruption and prevent such proceeds from remaining hidden in the United States.The case also required Obiang to disclose and remove other assets he owned in the United States. It further stipulated that if certain assets, including a Gulfstream jet, were ever brought into the country, they could be subject to seizure and forfeiture.A rapid flip and legal fightAfter the settlement, Obiang and the U.S. government selected luxury real estate broker Mauricio Umansky to handle the sale. Umansky, founder of The Agency and known to television audiences through his marriage to Kyle Richards of The Real Housewives of Beverly Hills, arranged a discreet transaction with developer Mauricio Oberfeld.The sale closed in June 2016 for a recorded price of $33.5 million, though later litigation described a $1 million repair credit that effectively lowered the price to $32.5 million. Oberfeld and his partners then invested heavily in renovations, with property records identifying a $26 million construction trust deed tied to the redevelopment.Just nine months later, in March 2017, the group sold the mansion for $69.9 million. That was more than double the original purchase price, and it set the stage for a lengthy legal dispute involving the original seller, Umansky, his business partners and another potential buyer.The litigation centered on allegations that Umansky failed to disclose information about another buyer’s willingness to pay more for the property. Umansky and The Agency denied wrongdoing, saying the sale was handled properly and that the mansion sold above its appraised value. The remaining claims were settled in December 2023, avoiding a civil trial.The latest $93.5 million saleThe estate was later owned by Malibu LaMalibu SA, a company registered in the British Virgin Islands and linked in reporting to Hong Kong heiress Karen Lo. That entity remained the recorded owner until the most recent transaction.On June 11, 2026, the property sold for $93.5 million, according to PropertyShark transaction data cited by Celebrity Net Worth. That is $23.6 million more than the $69.9 million sale in 2017, an increase of nearly 34 percent over nine years.The buyer was not initially disclosed. In November 2026, luxury real estate publication North Hillcrest reported that the buyer was the Stark family behind Chrome Hearts, although public property records do not independently identify the individual buyer.Chrome Hearts was founded by Richard Stark in 1988 and has become a major luxury brand known for silver jewelry, leather goods, sunglasses and gothic-inspired fashion. The company has remained largely family controlled, with Stark and his wife, Laurie Lynn, continuing to lead the business alongside their children.A growing Malibu portfolioThe reported purchase is not the Stark family’s first major Malibu investment. In 2017, Richard and Laurie Lynn paid $38.5 million for a 2.8-acre compound in Paradise Cove, and they later bought another Malibu home for $7.25 million.In November 2025, Chrome Hearts also purchased the Surfrider Hotel in Malibu for $37.5 million. The 20-room boutique hotel sits along Pacific Coast Highway, overlooking Surfrider Beach and the Malibu Pier.With the reported $93.5 million mansion acquisition, the combined purchase prices of the Paradise Cove estate, the Surfrider Hotel and the Sweetwater Mesa property reach $169.5 million. That figure underscores how deeply the family has invested in Malibu real estate.A property with a complicated pastThe Malibu estate’s journey reflects more than a simple rise in value. It began with a $30 million purchase by a government official whose salary could not plausibly support such spending, moved through a federal corruption settlement, then passed through a high-profile flip and years of litigation.Now, nearly two decades later, the property has sold again for $93.5 million. The latest reported buyer connection to Chrome Hearts adds another layer to the story, but it does not erase the estate’s unusual history.For Malibu, the sale is another example of the area’s extreme luxury market. For the people of Equatorial Guinea, however, the earlier settlement remains a reminder that even assets purchased with alleged corruption proceeds can be recovered and redirected toward public benefit.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? Vereadores vão analisar relatório que recomenda a perda do mandato do prefeito por supostas irregularidades no uso de R$ 2,1 milhões do Fundo Municipal de Transporte e Trânsito.

A vereadora Fran Miranda (PL), presidente da Comissão Processante, começou a leitura do relatório final, elaborado por ela e pelos vereadores Dani Galdino (Republicanos) e Pablo Fernandes (DC). O documento, de 78 páginas, recomenda a cassação do mandato do prefeito Yan Lopes (Podemos).

Na abertura dos trabalhos, o presidente da Câmara, Adilson Henrique (PL), explicou o motivo da sessão e pediu que fosse feita a leitura do relatório final da Comissão Processante, que recomenda a cassação do mandato do prefeito Yan Lopes.

O vereador Professor Maicon Goiembiesqui (Republicanos) fez a leitura de uma passagem da Bíblia no início da sessão, antes do início da análise do relatório que recomenda a cassação do prefeito Yan Lopes.

Nove dos 11 vereadores de Caçapava estão presentes na sessão que vai votar o pedido de cassação do prefeito Yan Lopes (Podemos). Não compareceram a vereadora Dandara Pereira Gissoni (PSB) e o vereador Rodrigo Meirelles (PL), que estão em viagem ao exterior.

A equipe da Câmara Municipal faz os últimos ajustes no plenário antes do início da sessão que vai votar o pedido de cassação do prefeito Yan Lopes. O espaço está sendo preparado para receber os vereadores, o prefeito e o público que acompanha o julgamento.

A sessão da Câmara Municipal de Caçapava, prevista para começar às 9h, está atrasada. Vereadores, o prefeito Yan Lopes e o público já estão no local à espera do início dos trabalhos, que vão decidir o pedido de cassação do mandato do prefeito. Até 9h15, a sessão ainda não havia começado.

O prefeito Yan Lopes (Podemos) chegou à Câmara Municipal de Caçapava para acompanhar a sessão que vai votar o pedido de cassação de seu mandato. Ele também deve apresentar pessoalmente sua defesa durante o julgamento.

A segurança também foi reforçada no entorno da Câmara Municipal. Viaturas da Guarda Civil Municipal (GCM) estão posicionadas no local para acompanhar a movimentação durante a sessão que vai votar o pedido de cassação do prefeito.

Antes de entrar na Câmara Municipal para acompanhar a sessão, o público precisou passar por um detector de metais e fazer um cadastro na entrada. As medidas foram adotadas como parte do controle de acesso ao plenário durante o julgamento do pedido de cassação do prefeito Yan Lopes.

Uma fila se formou do lado de fora da Câmara Municipal de Caçapava antes do início da sessão que vai votar o pedido de cassação do prefeito Yan Lopes. Desde antes das 8h o público aguardava para acompanhar o julgamento, marcado para começar às 9h desta terça-feira (10).

articles.title: Buying screenless tracker over smartwatch: Here's what you get and what you may miss
articles.summary: Picking a fitness wearable is no longer just a question of which brand to buy.
articles.body: Picking a fitness wearable is no longer just a question of which brand to buy. Today, you also have to decide whether you want a screen on your wrist or not at all. On one side is the screenless tracker, a slim, lightweight device that quietly collects data, and the form factor has gained popularity in recent months. Recently, Whoop, Google (Fitbit Air), Noise and other companies have launched these discrete fitness trackers.On the other hand is the smartwatch, which works as an extension of your smartphone while tracking your daily activity. Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4, Samsung Galaxy Ultra 2 and Galaxy Watch 9, and Google Pixel Watch 5 are some of the flagship products in the market. Both can help you keep an eye on your health, but they suit very different lifestyles. Here is a clear look at what you gain and what you give up with each one.What a screenless tracker offersA screenless tracker does exactly what the name suggests. There is no display, so there is nothing to light up, buzz or ping while you go about your day. The device simply collects data and you look at it later on a smartphone app. For people tired of constant alerts, that can be a big relief.Where a screenless tracker winsNo digital distractions. As there are no notifications, buzzes or bright displays, nothing interrupts a conversation and nothing lights up at bedtime. You stay present with the people around you.Another advantage is that these screenless trackers have longer battery life. A screen uses a lot of power. Without one, these devices run anywhere from 5 days to a full month on a single charge. That means far fewer trips to the charger.Thirdly, higher comfort, all day and night. The slim and lightweight design makes a screenless tracker much easier to wear around the clock, especially while sleeping.Moreover, a screenless tracker allows you to flaunt your favourite wrist watch, so you get freedom to keep wearing your classic analog or luxury mechanical watch on your wrist.Where screenless tracker falls shortNo real-time workout stats. This means that you cannot check your live pace, elapsed time or heart-rate zones during a workout without pulling out your phone. For runners and gym-goers who like to adjust their effort on the go, this is a drawback.The second thing is there is no daily utility for those who lean towards smartwatches. Screenless trackers will not get quick timers, alarms, step displays or incoming call alerts.What a smartwatch offersSmartwatches, such as the Apple Watch, Wear OS models like the offerings from Samsung and Google, and other models including Amazfit, act as an extension of your smartphone while tracking your daily activity. They put information and controls right on your wrist.Where smartwatch winsThe first advantage is instant glanceability. You can check pace, heart rate, timers and rep counts mid-workout with a quick look at your wrist.There is also day-to-day convenience. A smartwatch lets you take calls, reply to quick texts, check calendar alerts and, in some countries, pay at checkout counters – all without reaching for your phone.Thirdly, standalone navigation and audio. Many models support built-in GPS and offline music storage. That means you can leave your phone at home for outdoor runs.Where smartwatch falls shortOne of the drawbacks is frequent charging. Many full-featured smartwatches last about a day or two, which forces regular top-ups. Those charging breaks can disrupt continuous sleep tracking.Some people have constant screen distractions. Alerts and pings can be disruptive while you're working out, working or resting.Lastly, the rigid casing and glass screen can feel intrusive or uncomfortable to sleep in.Quick comparisonScreenless trackerSmartwatchBattery lifeLonger18 to 36 hours on many full-featured modelsDistractionsNoneAlerts and pingsLive workout statsNot available without your phoneOn your wristSleep comfortSlim and lightweightCan feel bulkyDaily utilityNo timers, alarms or call alertsCalls, texts, calendar alerts, paymentsWhich one should you choose?Choose a screenless tracker if you want a device that stays out of your way. It suits people who want fewer digital distractions, a slim and lightweight device to sleep in and a battery that needs charging only once every few days. It also works well if you love your analog or mechanical watch and do not want to give it up.Choose a smartwatch if you want information and tools on your wrist. It is the better fit if you like to see your pace and heart rate mid-workout, handle calls and quick texts, pay at checkout counters, or head out for outdoor runs without your phone. In return, you will need to charge it often, and its screen will keep competing for your attention.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.body: A hillside home in Los Angeles has received an extensive makeover, transforming from a dated Mediterranean-style property into a contemporary retreat with carefully selected natural finishes, upgraded amenities and a redesigned outdoor space. Behind the renovation is longtime music executive Bob Cavallo, whose career has included managing some of the music industry's biggest names. According to Mansion Global report, after purchasing the property for $2.75 million in March, Cavallo has now listed the revamped residence for just under $5 million.From music management to real estateCavallo's professional journey has spanned several decades and industries. He has managed celebrated acts including Prince, Earth, Wind & Fire, the Lovin' Spoonful, the Goo Goo Dolls and Alanis Morissette. His involvement in the entertainment business also extended to film production, including the iconic musical drama Purple Rain, the online report explains.He later played an important role in reorganising Walt Disney's music and concert operations into Disney Music Group. The division found considerable success during the early 2000s, working with young performers such as Hilary Duff, Miley Cyrus and the Jonas Brothers.According to Mansion Global, Cavallo originally purchased the Nichols Canyon property for a family member. When those plans changed, he decided to undertake a comprehensive renovation before putting the house back on the market.A complete transformationBuilt in 1988, the 3,762-square-foot residence had four bedrooms but retained interiors that appeared largely untouched for around two decades. Angie Williams of Nourmand & Associates, who handled the renovation through her home improvement company House of Renovo, oversaw the property's transformation.According to online reports, the colour scheme was kept largely neutral, allowing the natural materials and architectural details to stand out. One element that remained was the kitchen cabinetry, which had been replaced relatively recently and featured a dark taupe finish that complemented the redesigned interiors.An unusual addition improves accessibilityOne of the property's most interesting upgrades involved installing an elevator using an existing dumbwaiter shaft. Since the house is constructed into a hillside, its principal living areas sit on floors above the garage entrance. The addition provides a more convenient way to navigate the different levels.The renovation also extended to the building's exterior, which received new stucco, alongside a complete roof replacement.A landscaped backyard retreatThe outdoor areas received an equally substantial makeover. Previously, the backyard's deteriorating wooden decking had become a safety concern. Instead of replacing it with another uniform surface, the renovation introduced three distinct zones.A gravel area accommodates a fire pit, while a flagstone patio connects the outdoor kitchen and dining space. Artificial turf surrounds the swimming pool, creating a softer setting for relaxation.Surrounded by mature trees and greenery, the backyard offers a secluded atmosphere despite the property's proximity to Studio City, West Hollywood and Beverly Hills.According to Mansipn Global, with its extensive upgrades, hillside setting and redesigned interiors, Cavallo's Los Angeles property is now being marketed for nearly $5 million, representing a significant premium over its March purchase price.Images Courtesy: Alchetron and istockReady to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.summary: President Trump called in to the first episode of C-SPAN’s new show late Monday, addressing topics like immigration and a GOP-led effort to impeach his Defense secretary. “Washington Journal Primetime” host Mimi Geerges asked Trump about his recent comment that his administration’s massive deportation crackdown “might be too tough” after Republicans suffered significant losses in…
articles.body:
President Trump called in to the first episode of C-SPAN’s new show late Monday, addressing topics like immigration and a GOP-led effort to impeach his Defense secretary.

“Washington Journal Primetime” host Mimi Geerges asked Trump about his recent comment that his administration’s massive deportation crackdown “ might be too tough ” after Republicans suffered significant losses in the midterm elections.

The president defended these efforts as being focused on preventing the “worst of the worst” immigrants from residing in the U.S.

“We haven’t put the same pressure on waitresses and on farm workers, etc.,” he said. “Not even close.”

Geerges also pressed him on GOP Rep. Thomas Massie’s (Ky.) effort to oust Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. Massie filed eight articles of impeachment Monday, accusing the secretary of violating the Constitution and federal law during U.S. military operations in Iran and in other conflicts.

Trump has defended his Pentagon chief and said he “would be disappointed” if House Republicans voted in favor of the resolution.

“Look, Pete has won two wars. He’s been the head person in two wars,” the president said, touting the U.S. military operations in Venezuela and Iran.

Last week, he told ABC News’s Jonathan Karl he had “ every intention ” of keeping the Defense secretary in his Cabinet.

However, Trump also acknowledged in the interview that it would be easier to push through Hegseth’s replacement before Democrats take control of Congress next year, noting the secretary’s reported interest in Tennessee Sen. Marsha Blackburn’s (R) Senate seat.

On Tuesday morning, the president reiterated his support for Hegseth, after the secretary addressed the impeachment proceedings during a press conference .

“Pete Hegseth gets an ‘A’ PLUS, PLUS, PLUS for his defense against a disgruntled, angry, defeated, former Congressman, Thomas Massie, a TOTAL LOSER!” Trump wrote on Truth Social .

articles.title: Iran accuses US of ‘manufacturing fake news about imaginary talks’
articles.summary: Iran’s secretary of the Supreme National Security Council on Monday accused the U.S. of “manufacturing fake news about imaginary talks” to end the war, with President Trump downplaying the likelihood of renewed strikes amid talks with Qatar. “The war on Iran has already wrecked the US government,” Secretary Mohsen Rezaei said on the social platform X.…
articles.body:
Iran’s secretary of the Supreme National Security Council on Monday accused the U.S. of “manufacturing fake news about imaginary talks” to end the war, with President Trump downplaying the likelihood of renewed strikes amid talks with Qatar.

“The war on Iran has already wrecked the US government,” Secretary Mohsen Rezaei said on the social platform X . “But Washington flails like a desperate gambler. FOLD YOUR HAND. STOP manufacturing FAKE NEWS about imaginary talks. Stop denying the West Asian NEW ORDER.”

Rezaei called on the U.S. to “SURRENDER to the seven conditions Iran has repeatedly set out.”

Iran has offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, which it has effectively shut off since the start of the conflict, if the U.S. agreed to its seven conditions to end the fighting. These conditions include lifting sanctions and releasing billions of dollars in frozen Iranian assets.

But Trump and his administration have rejected these conditions, with Secretary of State Marco Rubio pushing back on Iran’s requests while in Paris on Tuesday.

“Iran is demanding reparations. They should be the ones paying reparations because they’re the ones that have destabilized the region for long periods of time,” he told reporters. “They’re demanding pallets of cash, which the president’s made clear is not going to happen.”

Rubio added that if Iran wants a nuclear energy program, “they should have one like many other countries around the world have” but there are “things they can do” to get to that point.

“Now, I think they want a deal, there’s no doubt they’d like a deal too, but they’re just not ready to make one, apparently,” he said. “But we’re open to it.”

Trump downplayed his pre-midterm election suggestion that he would renew strikes on Iran after the midterms, despite reported strikes on Qeshm Island last Monday and last Friday . Following the attacks, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi gave the U.S. an ultimatum after Tehran submitted a two-day proposal to end the conflict.

This downplay from the president during a White House press conference on Monday included Trump’s claim that the war was “ending quickly,” but that the U.S. wants “to take care of people that have been very good to us over the years,” referring to allies in the region.

These remarks followed a White House meeting with Qatar’s Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, who has served as the lead mediator between Washington and Tehran.

The administration has largely said the Iran war had a role in the sweeping Republican losses during the midterms. The conflict contributed to inflation and caused gas prices to soar, but high gas prices hit below $4 for the first time since July.
